translations.literal: Roll two hundred five
translations.idiomatic: Volume 205

sentences.zh: 【唐紀二十一】　起玄黓執徐，盡柔兆涒灘，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 21] From Xuanyi Zhixu through Rouzhao Tuantan; five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 21] From Xuanyi Zhixu through Rouzhao Tuantan—five years in all.

sentences.zh: 正月，戊辰朔，太后享萬象神宮。

translations.literal: In the first month, on the wuchen new moon, the Empress Dowager offered sacrifice at the Temple of Myriad Images.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, on the wuchen new moon, Empress Dowager Wu offered sacrifice at the Temple of Myriad Images.

sentences.zh: 臘月，立故于闐王尉遲伏闍雄之子瑕為于闐王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, they installed Xia, son of the former King of Khotan Yuchi Fuzhixiong, as King of Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Xia, son of the former King of Khotan Yuchi Fuzhixiong, was installed as King of Khotan.

sentences.zh: 春，一月，丁卯，太后引見存撫使所舉人，無問賢愚，悉加擢用，高者試鳳閣舍人、給事中，次試員外郎、侍御史、補闕、拾遺、校書郎。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dingmao, the Empress Dowager received those recommended by the commissioners for relief and comfort; without asking whether they were worthy or foolish, she promoted them all. The highest were tried as Fengge Attendants-in-Ordinary and Supervising Secretaries; the next as Outside Section Members, Attendant Censors, Remonstrance Officials, Petitioners, and Proofreaders.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dingmao, Empress Dowager Wu received everyone recommended by the relief commissioners. Without distinguishing talent from mediocrity, she promoted them all—the best as probationary Fengge Attendants-in-Ordinary and Supervising Secretaries, the rest as probationary Outside Section Members, Attendant Censors, Remonstrance Officials, Petitioners, and Proofreaders.

sentences.zh: 試官自此始。

translations.literal: Probationary appointments began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Probationary appointments began at this time.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「補闕連車載，拾遺平斗量；

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying of it: "Remonstrance Officials fill carts in succession; Petitioners are measured by the dou level;
translations.idiomatic: People of the time had a saying: "Remonstrance Officials fill cart after cart; Petitioners are measured out by the bushel;

sentences.zh: 欋推侍御史，碗脫校書郎。」

translations.literal: push with a winch for Attendant Censors, bowl off for Proofreaders."
translations.idiomatic: winch out Attendant Censors, ladle off Proofreaders."

sentences.zh: 有舉人沈全交續之曰：「心存撫使，瞇目聖神皇。」

translations.literal: A candidate, Shen Quanjiao, continued it: "The relief commissioner squints his eyes at the Holy and Divine Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: One candidate, Shen Quanjiao, added: "The relief commissioner squints at the Holy and Divine Emperor."

sentences.zh: 為御史紀先知所擒，劾其誹謗朝政，請杖之朝堂，然後付法，太后笑曰：「但使卿輩不濫，何恤人言！

translations.literal: He was seized by the censor Ji Xianzhi, who impeached him for slandering court policy and asked that he be beaten in the court hall and then handed over to the law. The Empress Dowager laughed and said, "So long as you gentlemen do not abuse your offices, why worry about what people say!
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Ji Xianzhi seized him, impeached him for slandering government policy, and asked that he be flogged in the court hall before being handed to the law. The Empress Dowager laughed and said, "So long as you gentlemen do not abuse your offices, why worry what people say!

sentences.zh: 宜釋其罪。」

translations.literal: His offense should be released."
translations.idiomatic: Release him from punishment."

sentences.zh: 先知大慚。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 太后雖濫以祿位收天下人心，然不稱職者，尋亦黜之，或加刑誅。

translations.literal: Although the Empress Dowager lavished salary and rank to win the hearts of all under Heaven, those unfit for office were soon dismissed, and some were even punished or executed.
translations.idiomatic: Though she lavished offices and salaries to win hearts across the realm, those unfit for their posts were soon removed—and some were punished or executed.

sentences.zh: 挾刑賞之柄以駕御天下，政由己出，明察善斷，故當時英賢亦競為之用。

translations.literal: Wielding the handles of punishment and reward to drive all under Heaven, with policy issuing from herself, clear-sighted and decisive in judgment, the worthy and able of the time also competed to serve her.
translations.idiomatic: Holding the levers of punishment and reward to govern the realm, with policy flowing from her alone, she was perceptive and decisive—so the able and eminent of the day also strove to serve her.

sentences.zh: 寧陵丞廬江郭霸以謅諛干太后，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Guo Ba, magistrate of Ningling from Lujiang, won the Empress Dowager through flattery and was appointed Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ba, magistrate of Ningling in Lujiang, won favor with the Empress Dowager through flattery and was appointed Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 中丞魏元忠病，霸往問之，因嘗其糞，喜曰：「大夫糞甘則可憂；

translations.literal: When Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong fell ill, Ba went to inquire after him and tasted his stool, saying with delight, "When a great man's stool is sweet there is cause for worry;
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong fell ill, Ba visited him, tasted his stool, and said with delight, "When a great man's stool is sweet, that is worrisome;

sentences.zh: 今苦，無傷也。」

translations.literal: now it is bitter—no harm done."
translations.idiomatic: now that it is bitter, there is no harm."

sentences.zh: 元忠大惡之，遇人輒告之。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong detested him greatly and told everyone he met about it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong loathed him and told everyone he met what had happened.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以夏官尚書楊執柔同平章事。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Yang Zhirou, Minister of the Summer Office, was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Yang Zhirou, Minister of the Summer Office, was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 執柔，恭仁弟之孫也，太后以外族用之。

translations.literal: Zhirou was a grandson of Yang Gongren's younger brother; the Empress Dowager employed him as a maternal relative.
translations.idiomatic: Zhirou was a grandson of Yang Gongren's younger brother; the Empress Dowager appointed him because of his maternal kinship.

sentences.zh: 初，隋煬帝作東都，無外城，僅有短垣而已，至是，鳳閣侍郎李昭德始築之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Yang of Sui built the Eastern Capital, there was no outer city—only a short wall. At this time Fengge Vice Minister Li Zhaode began to build it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang of Sui built the Eastern Capital, there had been no outer city—only a low wall. Now Fengge Vice Minister Li Zhaode began constructing the outer walls.

sentences.zh: 左台中丞來俊臣羅告同平章事任知古、狄仁傑、裴行本、司農卿裴宣禮、前文昌左丞盧獻、御史中丞魏元忠、潞州刺史李嗣真謀反。

translations.literal: Left Platform Vice Censor-in-Chief Lai Junchen fabricated charges that Associate Directors Ren Zhigu, Di Renjie, Pei Xingben, Minister of Agriculture Pei Xuanli, former Left Assistant Director of the Palace Library Lu Xian, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong, and Prefect of Lu Prefecture Li Sizhen had plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Left Platform Vice Censor-in-Chief Lai Junchen fabricated charges of treason against Associate Directors Ren Zhigu, Di Renjie, and Pei Xingben, Minister of Agriculture Pei Xuanli, former Left Assistant Director of the Palace Library Lu Xian, Vice Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong, and Prefect of Lu Prefecture Li Sizhen.

sentences.zh: 先是，來俊臣奏請降敕，一問即承反者得減死。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lai Junchen had memorialized requesting an imperial decree that whoever confessed to rebellion upon the first questioning should have death reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lai Junchen had asked for an edict granting commutation of the death penalty to anyone who confessed to treason at the first questioning.

sentences.zh: 及知古等下獄，俊臣以此誘之，仁傑對曰：「大周革命，萬物惟新，唐室舊臣，甘從誅戮。

translations.literal: When Zhigu and the others were cast into prison, Junchen used this to entice them. Renjie replied, "The Great Zhou has transformed the realm; all things are renewed. As an old servant of the Tang house, I am willing to accept execution.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhigu and the others were imprisoned, Junchen used this to entice them. Renjie replied, "The Great Zhou has transformed the realm; all things are made new. As an old servant of the Tang house, I am willing to accept execution.

sentences.zh: 反是實！」

translations.literal: Rebellion is the truth!"
translations.idiomatic: Treason is the truth!"

sentences.zh: 俊臣乃少寬之。

translations.literal: Junchen then relaxed the pressure somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen then eased the pressure somewhat.

sentences.zh: 判官王德壽謂仁傑曰：「尚書定減死矣。

translations.literal: The examining judge Wang Deshou said to Renjie, "Minister, your death sentence is certainly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Examining judge Wang Deshou said to Renjie, "Minister, your death sentence is certainly commuted.

sentences.zh: 德壽業受驅策，欲求少階級，煩尚書引楊執柔，可乎？」

translations.literal: Desou has long been driven about and wishes to gain a small step in rank. Might the Minister please implicate Yang Zhirou—would that be acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: I have long been driven about and wish to advance a step in rank. Would the Minister please implicate Yang Zhirou?"

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「皇天后土遣狄仁傑為如此事！」

translations.literal: Renjie said, "Heaven and Earth sent Di Renjie to do such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said, "Heaven and Earth sent Di Renjie to do such a thing!"

sentences.zh: 以頭觸柱，血流被面；

translations.literal: He struck his head against a pillar until blood covered his face;
translations.idiomatic: He struck his head against a pillar until blood covered his face;

sentences.zh: 德壽懼而謝之。

translations.literal: Desou was afraid and apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: Desou was frightened and apologized.

sentences.zh: 侯思止鞫魏元忠，元忠辭氣不屈；

translations.literal: Hou Sizhi interrogated Wei Yuanzhong; Yuanzhong's words and bearing did not yield;
translations.idiomatic: Hou Sizhi interrogated Wei Yuanzhong, whose words and bearing did not yield;

sentences.zh: 思止怒，命倒曳之。

translations.literal: Sizhi grew angry and ordered him dragged head downward.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi grew angry and ordered him dragged head downward.

sentences.zh: 元忠曰：「我薄命，譬如墜驢，足絓於鐙，為所曳耳。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong said, "I am of slight fate—like a fallen donkey whose foot is caught in the stirrup and is dragged along.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong said, "I am ill-fated—like a donkey that has fallen with its foot caught in the stirrup and is being dragged along.

sentences.zh: 思止愈怒，更曳之，元忠曰：「侯思止，汝若須魏元忠頭則截取，何必使承反也！」

translations.literal: Sizhi grew still angrier and dragged him further. Yuanzhong said, "Hou Sizhi, if you need Wei Yuanzhong's head, then cut it off—why must you make me confess rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi grew still angrier and dragged him further. Yuanzhong said, "Hou Sizhi, if you want Wei Yuanzhong's head, cut it off—why must you make me confess treason!"

sentences.zh: 狄仁傑既承反，有司待報行刑，不復嚴備。

translations.literal: Since Di Renjie had confessed to rebellion, the authorities awaited report to carry out execution and no longer kept strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: Once Di Renjie had confessed to treason, the authorities awaited orders to execute him and no longer kept strict guard.

sentences.zh: 仁傑裂衾帛書冤狀，置綿衣中，謂王德壽曰：「天時方熱，請授家人去其綿。」

translations.literal: Renjie tore quilted silk and wrote a petition of injustice, placed it inside his padded garment, and said to Wang Deshou, "The season is hot—please let my family take away the padding."
translations.idiomatic: Renjie tore cloth from his quilt and wrote a petition of injustice, hid it in his padded garment, and said to Wang Deshou, "The weather is hot—please let my family remove the padding."

sentences.zh: 德壽許之。

translations.literal: Desou consented.
translations.idiomatic: Desou agreed.

sentences.zh: 仁傑子光遠得書，持之稱變，得召見。

translations.literal: Renjie's son Guangyuan obtained the letter, presented it claiming an emergency, and was granted an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie's son Guangyuan obtained the letter, presented it as an urgent petition, and was granted an audience.

sentences.zh: 則天覽之，以問俊臣，對曰：「仁傑等下獄，臣未嘗褫其巾帶，寢處甚安，苟無事實，安肯承反！」

translations.literal: Zetian read it and questioned Junchen. He replied, "When Renjie and the others were imprisoned, I never removed their caps and belts; they slept very comfortably. If there were no facts, how would they confess rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian read it and questioned Junchen. He replied, "When Renjie and the others were imprisoned, I never removed their caps and belts; they slept comfortably. If there were no truth to the charges, why would they confess treason!"

sentences.zh: 太后使通事舍人周絲林往視之，俊臣暫假仁傑等巾帶，羅立於西，使絲林視之；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager sent Palace Service Gentleman Zhou Silin to inspect them. Junchen temporarily lent Renjie and the others their caps and belts and had them stand in a row to the west for Silin to view;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager sent Palace Service Gentleman Zhou Silin to inspect them. Junchen temporarily restored their caps and belts and had them stand in a row to the west for Silin to see;

sentences.zh: 絲林不敢視，唯東顧唯諾而已。

translations.literal: Silin dared not look; he only turned east and murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: Silin dared not look; he only turned east and murmured assent.

sentences.zh: 俊臣又詐為仁傑等謝死表，使絲林奏之。

translations.literal: Junchen also forged for Renjie and the others petitions thanking for death and had Silin present them.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen also forged petitions thanking for death on behalf of Renjie and the others and had Silin present them.

sentences.zh: 樂思晦男未十歲，沒入司農，上變，得召見。

translations.literal: The son of Yue Sihui, not yet ten years old, was confiscated into the Ministry of Agriculture. He submitted an urgent report and was granted an audience.
translations.idiomatic: The son of Yue Sihui, not yet ten years old, had been confiscated as a bondsman of the Ministry of Agriculture. He submitted an urgent report and was granted an audience.

sentences.zh: 太后問狀，對曰：「臣父已死，臣家已破，但惜陛下法為俊臣等所弄。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager asked the circumstances. He replied, "My father is already dead and my family already ruined, but I grieve that Your Majesty's law is being toyed with by Junchen and his like.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager asked what had happened. He replied, "My father is dead and my family ruined, but I grieve that Your Majesty's law is being manipulated by Junchen and his ilk.

sentences.zh: 陛下不信臣言，乞擇朝臣之忠清、陛下素所信任者，為反狀以付俊臣，無不承反矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not believe my words, I beg you choose a court official who is loyal and pure and whom Your Majesty has always trusted, draw up a charge of rebellion and hand it to Junchen—none will fail to confess rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not believe me, choose any loyal and upright courtier whom you have always trusted, draw up a charge of treason and hand it to Junchen—none will fail to confess."

sentences.zh: 太后意稍寤，召見仁傑等，問曰：「卿承反何也？

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's mind was somewhat awakened. She summoned Renjie and the others and asked, "Why did you confess rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager's mind was somewhat awakened. She summoned Renjie and the others and asked, "Why did you confess treason?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「不承，則已死於拷掠矣。」

translations.literal: They replied, "Had we not confessed, we would already have died under torture."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Had we not confessed, we would already have died under torture."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「何為作謝死表？」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "Why did you write petitions thanking for death?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Why did you write petitions thanking for death?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「無之。」

translations.literal: They replied, "We did not."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "We did not."

sentences.zh: 出表示之，乃知其詐，於是出此七族。

translations.literal: The petitions were produced and shown them; then she knew of the fraud, and at this released these seven clans.
translations.idiomatic: The petitions were produced and shown to them; then she knew of the fraud, and released these seven men and their families.

sentences.zh: 庚午，貶知古江夏令，仁傑彭澤令，宣禮夷陵令，元忠涪陵令，獻西鄉令；

translations.literal: On gengwu, Zhigu was demoted to Magistrate of Jiangxia, Renjie to Magistrate of Pengze, Xuanli to Magistrate of Yiling, Yuanzhong to Magistrate of Fuling, and Xian to Magistrate of Xixiang;
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Zhigu was demoted to Magistrate of Jiangxia, Renjie to Magistrate of Pengze, Xuanli to Magistrate of Yiling, Yuanzhong to Magistrate of Fuling, and Xian to Magistrate of Xixiang;

sentences.zh: 流行本、嗣真於嶺南。

translations.literal: Xingben and Sizhen were exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Xingben and Sizhen were exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 俊臣與武承嗣等固請誅之，太后不許。

translations.literal: Junchen and Wu Chengsi and others firmly requested their execution; the Empress Dowager did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen, Wu Chengsi, and others pressed for their execution, but the Empress Dowager refused.

sentences.zh: 俊臣乃獨稱行本罪尤重，請誅之；

translations.literal: Junchen then alone declared Xingben's offense especially grave and requested his execution;
translations.idiomatic: Junchen then alone declared that Xingben's offense was especially grave and requested his execution;

sentences.zh: 秋官郎中徐有功駁之，以為：「明主有更生之恩，俊臣不能將順，虧損恩信。」

translations.literal: Autumn Office Director Xu Yougong rebutted him, stating: "A enlightened ruler has the grace to grant new life. Junchen cannot follow and accommodate this, damaging grace and trust."
translations.idiomatic: Autumn Office Director Xu Yougong objected, saying, "An enlightened ruler has the grace to grant new life. Junchen cannot follow her will in this, damaging her grace and credibility."

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史貴鄉霍獻可，宣禮之甥也，言於太后曰：「陛下不殺裴宣禮，臣請隕命於前。」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censor Huo Xianke of Guixiang, a nephew of Xuanli, said to the Empress Dowager, "If Your Majesty does not execute Pei Xuanli, I request to lay down my life before you."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Censor Huo Xianke of Guixiang, Xuanli's nephew, said to the Empress Dowager, "If Your Majesty does not execute Pei Xuanli, I beg to lay down my life before you."

sentences.zh: 以頭觸殿階，血流沾地，以示為人臣不私其親。

translations.literal: He struck his head against the palace steps until blood stained the ground, to show that as a minister he did not favor his kin.
translations.idiomatic: He struck his head against the palace steps until blood stained the ground, to show that as a minister he did not favor his kin.

sentences.zh: 太后皆不聽。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager would not heed any of them.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager would not heed any of them.

sentences.zh: 獻可常以綠帛裹其傷，微露之於帕頭下，冀太后見之以為忠。

translations.literal: Xianke often wrapped his wound in green silk and slightly exposed it beneath his headcloth, hoping the Empress Dowager would see it and regard him as loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke often wrapped his wound in green silk and slightly exposed it beneath his headcloth, hoping the Empress Dowager would see it and regard him as loyal.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，補闕薛謙光上疏，以為：「選舉之法，宜得實才，取捨之間，風化所繫。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Remonstrance Official Xue Qianguang submitted a memorial, stating: "The method of selection should obtain real talent; in the choice between taking and leaving lies what custom and transformation depend on.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Remonstrance Official Xue Qianguang submitted a memorial stating, "The selection system should secure genuine talent; what is chosen and what is rejected shapes the moral tone of the age.

sentences.zh: 今之選人，咸稱覓舉，奔競相尚，喧訴無慚。

translations.literal: Today's candidates all claim to be seeking recommendation; rushing and competing are honored, clamoring and pleading without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Today's candidates all boast of seeking recommendation; scrambling and competition are honored, and shameless clamoring for favor is the norm.

sentences.zh: 至於才應經邦，惟令試策；

translations.literal: As for talent fit to govern the state, they are only made to try policy essays;
translations.idiomatic: As for talent fit to govern the state, they are tested only by policy essays;

sentences.zh: 武能制敵，止驗彎弧。

translations.literal: military ability to overcome the enemy is verified only by bending the bow.
translations.idiomatic: military ability to overcome the enemy is judged only by archery.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武帝見司馬相如賦，恨不同時，及置之朝廷，終文園令，知其不堪公卿之任故也。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wu of Han saw Sima Xiangru's fu and regretted not living in the same age; yet when he placed him at court, he ended as Chief of Wenyuan—knowing he could not bear the duties of high ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han once read Sima Xiangru's fu and regretted not living in the same age; yet when he placed him at court, Xiangru ended as Chief of Wenyuan—knowing he was unfit for high ministerial office.

sentences.zh: 吳起將戰，左右進劍，起曰：『將者提鼓揮桴，臨敵決疑，一劍之任，非將事也。』

translations.literal: When Wu Qi was about to give battle, attendants at his side presented swords. Qi said, "A general raises the drum and wields the baton, faces the enemy and resolves doubts—a sword's task is not a general's business."
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Qi was about to give battle, attendants presented swords. He said, "A general raises the drum and wields the baton, faces the enemy and resolves doubts—a sword's task is not a general's business."

sentences.zh: 然則虛文豈足以佐時，善射豈足以克敵！

translations.literal: Thus empty literary display—how can it suffice to aid the age? Skill at shooting—how can it suffice to overcome the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: How then can empty literary display aid the age, or skill at archery overcome the enemy!

sentences.zh: 要在文吏察其行能，武吏觀其勇略，考居官之臧否，行舉者賞罰而已。」

translations.literal: What matters is that civil officials examine conduct and ability, military officials observe courage and strategy, assess good and ill in office, and reward and punish those who recommend—nothing more."
translations.idiomatic: What matters is that civil officials examine conduct and ability, military officials observe courage and strategy, assess performance in office, and reward and punish those who recommend—that is all."

sentences.zh: 來俊臣求金於左衛大將軍泉獻誠，不得，誣以謀反，下獄。

translations.literal: Lai Junchen sought gold from Left Guard General Quan Xiancheng and did not obtain it; he falsely charged him with plotting rebellion and cast him into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen demanded gold from Left Guard General Quan Xiancheng; when refused, he falsely charged him with treason and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，縊殺之。

translations.literal: On yihai, he was strangled to death.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, he was strangled to death.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，司刑卿、檢校陝州刺史李游道為冬官尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Director of the Office of Punishments and Acting Prefect of Shan Prefecture Li Youdao was made Minister of the Winter Office and Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Director of the Office of Punishments and Acting Prefect of Shan Prefecture Li Youdao was made Minister of the Winter Office and Associate Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 二月，己亥，吐蕃党項部落萬餘人內附，分置十州。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jihai, more than ten thousand persons of Tibetan and Tangut tribes submitted and were settled across ten prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jihai, more than ten thousand people of Tibetan and Tangut tribes submitted and were settled across ten prefectures.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以秋官尚書袁智弘同平章事。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Autumn Office Minister Yuan Zhihong was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Autumn Office Minister Yuan Zhihong was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙申，赦天下，改元如意。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingshen, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm and the era name was changed to Ruyi.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on bingshen, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Ruyi.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙寅，禁天下屠殺及捕魚蝦。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on bingyin, slaughter throughout the realm and the catching of fish and shrimp were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingyin, slaughter throughout the realm and the catching of fish and shrimp were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 江淮旱，饑，民不得采魚蝦，餓死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The Yangzi and Huai regions suffered drought and famine; the people could not gather fish and shrimp, and very many died of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi and Huai regions suffered drought and famine; barred from gathering fish and shrimp, vast numbers starved.

sentences.zh: 右拾遺張德，生男三日，私殺羊會同僚，補闕杜肅懷一餤，上表告之。

translations.literal: Right Petitioner Zhang De, three days after his son was born, privately slaughtered a sheep to feast his colleagues. Remonstrance Official Du Su carried away a piece of pastry in his bosom and submitted a memorial reporting him.
translations.idiomatic: Right Petitioner Zhang De, three days after his son was born, privately slaughtered a sheep to feast his colleagues. Remonstrance Official Du Su pocketed a piece of meat and submitted a memorial reporting him.

sentences.zh: 明日，太后對仗，謂德曰：「聞卿生男，甚喜。」

translations.literal: The next day, at court audience, the Empress Dowager said to De, "I hear you had a son—I am very pleased."
translations.idiomatic: The next day, at court audience, the Empress Dowager said to De, "I hear you had a son—I am very pleased."

sentences.zh: 德拜謝。

translations.literal: De bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: De bowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「何從得肉？」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "Where did you get meat?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Where did you get meat?"

sentences.zh: 德叩頭服罪。

translations.literal: De knocked his head and confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: De knocked his head to the ground and confessed.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「朕禁屠宰，吉凶不預。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "I forbid slaughter, but I do not interfere with auspicious and inauspicious occasions.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "I forbid slaughter, but I do not interfere with occasions of joy or mourning.

sentences.zh: 然卿自今召客，亦須擇人。」

translations.literal: Yet from now on when you invite guests, you must also choose your company."
translations.idiomatic: Yet from now on when you invite guests, you must also choose your company carefully."

sentences.zh: 出肅表示之。

translations.literal: She produced Su's memorial and showed it.
translations.idiomatic: She produced Su's memorial and showed it to him.

sentences.zh: 肅大慚，舉朝欲唾其面。

translations.literal: Su was greatly ashamed; the whole court wished to spit in his face.
translations.idiomatic: Su was deeply ashamed; the whole court wished to spit in his face.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃酋長曷蘇帥部落請內附，以右玉鈐衛將軍張玄遇為安撫使，將精卒二萬迎之。

translations.literal: Tibetan chieftain He Su led his tribe in requesting submission. Right Jade Bell Guard General Zhang Xuanyu was made Pacification Commissioner and led twenty thousand picked troops to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan chieftain He Su led his tribe in requesting submission. Right Jade Bell Guard General Zhang Xuanyu was appointed Pacification Commissioner and led twenty thousand picked troops to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 六月，軍至大渡水西，曷蘇事洩，為國人所擒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the army reached west of the Dadu River. He's Su's plan was exposed and he was seized by his countrymen.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, the army reached the west bank of the Dadu River. He's Su's plan was exposed and he was seized by his own people.

sentences.zh: 別部酋長昝捶帥羌蠻八千餘人內附，玄遇以其部落置萊川州而還。

translations.literal: Another branch chieftain, Zanchui, led more than eight thousand Qiang and barbarians in submission. Xuanyu settled their tribe as Laichuan Prefecture and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Another chieftain, Zanchui, led more than eight thousand Qiang and tribal peoples in submission. Xuanyu settled them as Laichuan Prefecture and returned.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，萬年主簿徐堅上疏，以為：「書有五聽之道，令著三覆之奏。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Chief Clerk of Wannian Xu Jian submitted a memorial, stating: "The classics set forth the Way of the Five Hearings; statutes prescribe the memorial of threefold review.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Chief Clerk of Wannian Xu Jian submitted a memorial stating, "The classics set forth the Way of the Five Hearings; statutes prescribe threefold review of capital cases.

sentences.zh: 竊見比有敕推按反者，令使者得實，即行斬決。

translations.literal: I have observed that recently there have been edicts to investigate rebels, ordering that when envoys obtain the facts, execution by beheading is carried out at once.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that recent edicts on investigating rebels order immediate execution once envoys obtain confessions.

sentences.zh: 人命至重，死不再生，萬一懷枉，吞聲赤族，豈不痛哉！

translations.literal: Human life is supremely weighty; once dead it does not live again. If by any chance one harbors injustice, silenced and with his whole clan destroyed—how is that not anguish!
translations.idiomatic: Human life is supremely precious; death cannot be undone. If even one innocent man is silenced and his whole clan destroyed—how is that not anguish!

sentences.zh: 此不足肅奸逆而明典刑，適所以長威福而生疑懼。

translations.literal: This is insufficient to awe traitors and clarify penal law; it only lengthens arbitrary power and breeds suspicion and fear.
translations.idiomatic: This does not awe traitors or clarify the law; it only extends arbitrary power and breeds suspicion and fear.

sentences.zh: 臣望絕此處分，依法覆奏。

translations.literal: Your servant hopes this practice may be ended and review memorials submitted according to law.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that this practice be ended and that cases be reviewed and memorialized according to law.

sentences.zh: 又，法官之任，宜加簡擇，有用法寬平，為百姓所稱者，願親而任之；

translations.literal: Moreover, in the appointment of judicial officers there should be careful selection: those who apply the law with breadth and fairness and are praised by the common people—may they be drawn close and employed;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, judicial officers should be carefully chosen: those who apply the law with breadth and fairness and are praised by the people should be favored and employed;

sentences.zh: 有處事深酷，不允人望者，願疏而退之。」

translations.literal: those who handle affairs with deep harshness and do not accord with people's hopes—may they be kept at a distance and removed.
translations.idiomatic: those who handle affairs with deep harshness and fail to win public trust should be kept at a distance and removed.

sentences.zh: 堅，齊聃之子也。

translations.literal: Jian was a son of Qi Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was a son of Qi Dan.

sentences.zh: 夏官侍郎李昭德密言於太后曰：「魏王承嗣權太重。」

translations.literal: Summer Office Vice Minister Li Zhaode spoke secretly to the Empress Dowager, saying, "Prince of Wei Chengsi's power is too great."
translations.idiomatic: Summer Office Vice Minister Li Zhaode spoke privately to the Empress Dowager, saying, "Prince of Wei Chengsi's power is too great."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「吾侄也，故委以腹心。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "He is my nephew, so I have entrusted him with my innermost affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "He is my nephew, so I have entrusted him with my innermost confidence."

sentences.zh: 昭德曰：「侄之於姑，其親何如子之於父？

translations.literal: Zhaode said, "Between nephew and paternal aunt, how can kinship compare with that between son and father?
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode said, "How can the bond between nephew and paternal aunt compare with that between son and father?

sentences.zh: 子猶有篡弒其父者，況侄乎！

translations.literal: Even sons have usurped and murdered their fathers—how much more so nephews!
translations.idiomatic: Even sons have usurped and murdered their fathers—how much more so nephews!

sentences.zh: 今承嗣既陛下之侄，為親王，又為宰相，權侔人主，臣恐陛下不得久安天位也！」

translations.literal: Now Chengsi is both Your Majesty's nephew, a prince, and a chancellor; his power rivals that of the sovereign. Your servant fears Your Majesty may not long keep the throne in peace!"
translations.idiomatic: Now Chengsi is Your Majesty's nephew, a prince, and a chancellor—his power rivals the sovereign's. I fear Your Majesty may not long keep the throne in peace!"

sentences.zh: 太后矍然曰：「朕未之思。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager started and said, "I had not thought of that."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager started and said, "I had not considered that."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊寅，以文昌左相、同鳳閣鸞台三品武承嗣為特進，納言武攸寧為冬官尚書，夏官尚書、同平章事楊執柔為地官尚書，並罷政事；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuyin, Left Director of the Palace Library and Third-Rank Associate of Fengge and Luantai Wu Chengsi was made Special Advancement; Edict Attendant Wu Youning was made Minister of the Winter Office; Summer Office Minister and Associate Director Yang Zhirou was made Minister of the Earth Office—all were removed from government affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on wuyin, Wu Chengsi was made Special Advancement and removed from the chancellery; Wu Youning was made Minister of the Winter Office; Yang Zhirou was made Minister of the Earth Office—all were stripped of policy-making power;

sentences.zh: 以秋官侍郎新鄭崔元綜為鸞台侍郎，夏官侍郎李昭德為鳳閣侍郎，檢校天官侍郎姚璹為文昌左丞，檢校地官侍郎李元素為文昌右丞，與司賓卿崔神基並同平章事。

translations.literal: Autumn Office Vice Minister Cui Yuanzong of Xinzheng was made Luantai Vice Minister; Summer Office Vice Minister Li Zhaode was made Fengge Vice Minister; Acting Personnel Office Vice Minister Yao Shuo was made Left Assistant Director of the Palace Library; Acting Earth Office Vice Minister Li Yuansu was made Right Assistant Director of the Palace Library; and Director of Guests Cui Shenji—all were made Associate Directors of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuanzong of Xinzheng was made Luantai Vice Minister; Li Zhaode was made Fengge Vice Minister; Yao Shuo was made Left Assistant Director of the Palace Library; Li Yuansu was made Right Assistant Director; and Cui Shenji—all were made Associate Directors of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: □，思廉之孫；

translations.literal: Shuo was a grandson of Silian;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuo was a grandson of Yao Silian;

sentences.zh: 元素，敬玄之弟也。

translations.literal: Yuansu was a younger brother of Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansu was a younger brother of Li Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以營繕大匠王璿為夏官尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Master Builder Wang Xuan was made Minister of the Summer Office and Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Master Builder Wang Xuan was made Minister of the Summer Office and Associate Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 承嗣亦毀昭德於太后，太后曰：「吾任昭德，始得安眠，此代吾勞，汝勿言也。」

translations.literal: Chengsi also slandered Zhaode to the Empress Dowager. She said, "I rely on Zhaode and can sleep peacefully; he takes my labor upon himself—you need say no more."
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi also slandered Zhaode to the Empress Dowager. She said, "I rely on Zhaode and can sleep in peace; he bears my burdens for me—say no more."

sentences.zh: 是時，酷吏恣橫，百官畏之側足，昭德獨廷奏其奸。

translations.literal: At this time the harsh officials ran rampant; the hundred officials feared them and walked on tiptoe, but Zhaode alone memorialized at court exposing their wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the harsh officials ran rampant; officials feared them and walked on tiptoe, but Zhaode alone exposed their crimes at court.

sentences.zh: 太后好祥瑞，有獻白石赤文者，執政詰其異，對曰：「以其赤心。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager loved auspicious omens. Someone presented white stone with red markings. The chief ministers questioned its strangeness; he replied, "Because of its red heart."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager loved auspicious omens. Someone presented white stone with red markings. The chief ministers questioned its strangeness; he replied, "Because of its red heart."

sentences.zh: 昭德怒曰：「此石赤心，他石盡反邪？」

translations.literal: Zhaode said angrily, "This stone has a red heart—are all other stones in rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode said angrily, "This stone has a red heart—are all other stones traitors?"

sentences.zh: 左右皆笑。

translations.literal: Those at her side all laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Those at her side all laughed.

sentences.zh: 襄州人胡慶以丹漆書龜腹曰：「天子萬萬年。」

translations.literal: Hu Qing of Xiang Prefecture wrote on a turtle's belly with cinnabar lacquer: "May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Qing of Xiang Prefecture wrote on a turtle's belly in cinnabar lacquer: "May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand ten thousand years."

sentences.zh: 諧闕獻之。

translations.literal: He went to the palace gate jestingly and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the palace gate in jest and presented it.

sentences.zh: 昭德以刀刮盡，奏請付法。

translations.literal: Zhaode scraped it all off with a knife and memorialized requesting that he be handed to the law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode scraped it all off with a knife and asked that he be handed to the law.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「此心亦無惡。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "This heart also harbors no evil."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "This heart also harbors no malice."

sentences.zh: 命釋之。

translations.literal: She ordered his release.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered his release.

sentences.zh: 太后習貓，使與鸚鵡共處，出示百官。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager had trained a cat and placed it together with a parrot to show the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager had trained a cat and placed it with a parrot to show the officials.

sentences.zh: 傳觀未遍，貓饑，搏鸚鵡食之，太后甚慚。

translations.literal: Before the viewing had gone around to all, the cat grew hungry, seized the parrot, and ate it. The Empress Dowager was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Before everyone had seen it, the hungry cat seized the parrot and ate it. The Empress Dowager was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 太后自垂拱以來，任用酷吏，先誅唐宗室貴戚數百人，次及大臣數百家，其刺史、郎將以下，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Since the Chuigong era the Empress Dowager had employed harsh officials, first executing several hundred Tang imperial clansmen and noble kin, then several hundred great ministers; prefects, commanders, and those below—beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Chuigong era she had employed harsh officials, first executing hundreds of Tang imperial clansmen and nobles, then hundreds of great ministers; prefects, commanders, and those below—beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 每除一官，戶婢竊相謂曰：「鬼樸又來矣。」

translations.literal: Whenever an official was appointed, household servants would whisper to one another, "The ghost club has come again."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an official was appointed, household servants would whisper, "The ghost club has come again."

sentences.zh: 不旬月，輒遭掩捕、族誅。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days he would suffer secret arrest and clan execution.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than ten days he would suffer secret arrest and clan execution.

sentences.zh: 監察御史朝邑嚴善思，公直敢言。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Yan Shansi of Chaoyi was upright and bold in speech.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Yan Shansi of Chaoyi was upright and bold in speech.

sentences.zh: 時告密者不可勝數，太后亦厭其煩，命善思按問，引虛伏罪者八百五十餘人。

translations.literal: Informers at the time were beyond counting; the Empress Dowager also grew weary of the nuisance and ordered Shansi to investigate. He exposed more than eight hundred fifty who had falsely confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Informers were beyond counting; the Empress Dowager grew weary and ordered Shansi to investigate. He exposed more than eight hundred fifty false confessions.

sentences.zh: 羅織之黨為之不振，乃相與共構陷善思，坐流歡州。

translations.literal: The faction that fabricated charges was thereby checked; they then jointly framed Shansi, who was exiled to Huan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The faction that fabricated charges was checked; they then framed Shansi, who was exiled to Huan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太后知其枉，尋復召為渾儀監丞。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager knew he had been wronged and soon recalled him as Director of the Armillary Sphere.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he had been wronged, she soon recalled him as Director of the Armillary Sphere.

sentences.zh: 善思名譔，以字行。

translations.literal: Shansi's given name was Zun; he was known by his style.
translations.idiomatic: Shansi's given name was Zun; he was known by his style name.

sentences.zh: 右補闕新鄭朱敬則以太后本任威刑以禁異議，今既革命，眾心已定，宜省刑尚寬，乃上疏，以為：「李斯相秦，用刻薄變詐以屠諸侯，不知易之以寬和，卒至土崩，此不知變之禍也。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Official Zhu Jingze of Xinzheng, noting that the Empress Dowager had originally relied on severe punishment to suppress dissent and that now the revolution was accomplished and popular hearts settled, held that punishments should be reduced and leniency honored. He submitted a memorial stating: "When Li Si served as chancellor of Qin, he used harshness and deceit to slaughter the feudal lords, not knowing to replace these with breadth and harmony, until the state collapsed—this is the disaster of not knowing how to change.
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrance Official Zhu Jingze of Xinzheng argued that since the Empress Dowager had originally relied on harsh punishment to suppress dissent and the revolution was now accomplished and hearts were settled, punishments should be reduced and leniency honored. He submitted a memorial: "When Li Si served Qin, he used harshness and deceit to destroy the feudal lords, not knowing to replace these with breadth and harmony, until the state collapsed—this is the disaster of failing to change.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖定天下，陸賈、叔孫通說之以禮義，傳世十二，此知變之善也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Han settled the realm, Lu Jia and Shusun Tong persuaded him with ritual and righteousness, and the line endured twelve generations—this is the good of knowing how to change.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu of Han settled the realm, Lu Jia and Shusun Tong persuaded him with ritual and righteousness, and the line endured twelve generations—this is the benefit of knowing how to change.

sentences.zh: 自文明草昧，天地屯蒙，三叔流言，四凶構難，不設鉤距，無以應天順人，不切刑名，不可摧奸息暴。

translations.literal: From the Weming era when the world was still obscure, heaven and earth in turmoil, the three uncles spreading slander and the four villains plotting trouble—without setting traps and probes one could not respond to Heaven and accord with the people; without applying penal law one could not crush treachery and quell violence.
translations.idiomatic: From the Weming era, when heaven and earth were in turmoil and the three uncles spread slander while the four villains plotted trouble—without traps and probes one could not respond to Heaven and accord with the people; without penal law one could not crush treachery and quell violence.

sentences.zh: 故置神器，開告端，曲直之影必呈，包藏之心盡露，神道助直，無罪不除，蒼生晏然，紫宸易主。

translations.literal: Therefore the sacred vessel was set in place, informers were opened, the shadow of right and wrong necessarily appeared, hearts of concealment were fully exposed, the divine way aided the upright, the guiltless were not spared, the common people were at peace, and the Purple Forbidden changed its master.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the throne was secured, informers were encouraged, right and wrong were exposed, hidden hearts were laid bare, the divine way aided the upright, the guilty were eliminated, the people were at peace, and the throne changed hands.

sentences.zh: 然而急趨無善跡，促柱少和聲，向時之妙策，乃當今之芻狗也。

translations.literal: Yet hurried steps leave no good tracks, and tightened pegs yield little harmonious sound; the clever policies of that time are but straw dogs for today.
translations.idiomatic: Yet hurried steps leave no good tracks, and tightened pegs yield little harmonious sound; the clever policies of that time are but straw dogs for today.

sentences.zh: 伏願覽秦、漢之得失，考時事之合宜，審糟粕之可遺，覺蘧廬之須毀，去萋菲之牙角，頓奸險之鋒芒，窒羅織之源，掃朋黨之跡，使天下蒼生坦然大悅，豈不樂哉！」

translations.literal: Your servant humbly hopes Your Majesty will survey the gains and losses of Qin and Han, examine what suits present affairs, discern what dregs may be discarded, perceive that the grass hut must be torn down, remove the thorns of slander, blunt the sharp edges of treachery, stop the springs of fabricated charges, sweep away the traces of faction, and let all the people under Heaven be openly and greatly pleased—would that not be joy!"
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will survey the gains and losses of Qin and Han, examine what suits present affairs, discard what is dross, tear down what is temporary, remove the thorns of slander, blunt the edges of treachery, stop the springs of fabricated charges, sweep away faction, and let all under Heaven be openly and greatly pleased—would that not be joy!"

sentences.zh: 太后善之，賜帛三百段。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager approved and bestowed three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager approved and bestowed three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 侍御史周矩上疏曰：「推劾之吏皆相矜以虐，泥耳籠頭，枷研楔轂，摺膺籤爪，懸發薰耳，號曰『獄持』。

translations.literal: Attendant Censor Zhou Ju submitted a memorial saying: "The examining officers all pride themselves on cruelty—mudding the ears, caging the head, cangue and wedge and pestle, folding the breast and pinning the nails, hanging by the hair and smoking the ears—called 'prison holding.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Zhou Ju submitted a memorial: "Examining officers pride themselves on cruelty—mudding the ears, caging the head, cangue and wedge and pestle, folding the breast and pinning the nails, hanging by the hair and smoking the ears—called 'prison holding.

sentences.zh: 或累日節食，連宵緩問，晝夜搖撼，使不得眠，號曰『宿囚』。

translations.literal: Some are deprived of food for days on end, questioned slowly night after night, shaken day and night so they cannot sleep—called 'overnight prisoners.'"
translations.idiomatic: Some are starved for days, questioned slowly night after night, shaken day and night so they cannot sleep—called 'overnight prisoners.'"

sentences.zh: 此等既非木石，且救目前，苟求賒死。

translations.literal: These men are not wood or stone; facing present peril, they seek only to postpone death.
translations.idiomatic: These men are not wood or stone; facing present peril, they seek only to postpone death.

sentences.zh: 臣竊聽輿議，皆稱天下太平，何苦須反！

translations.literal: Your servant has privately listened to public talk: all say the realm is at peace—why must one rebel!
translations.idiomatic: I have listened to public talk: all say the realm is at peace—why must one rebel!

sentences.zh: 豈被告者儘是英雄，欲求帝王邪？

translations.literal: Are all the accused heroes seeking to become emperors?
translations.idiomatic: Are all the accused heroes seeking to become emperors?

sentences.zh: 但不勝楚毒自誣耳。

translations.literal: They simply cannot bear Chu torture and falsely incriminate themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They simply cannot bear the torture and falsely incriminate themselves.

sentences.zh: 願陛下察之。

translations.literal: Your servant hopes Your Majesty will examine this.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to examine this.

sentences.zh: 今滿朝側息不安，皆以為陛下朝與之密，夕與之仇，不可保也。

translations.literal: Now the whole court holds its breath in unease, all thinking that those Your Majesty is intimate with in the morning are enemies by evening—no one is secure.
translations.idiomatic: Now the whole court holds its breath, thinking that those intimate with Your Majesty in the morning are enemies by evening—no one is secure.

sentences.zh: 周用仁而昌，秦用刑而亡。

translations.literal: Zhou employed benevolence and flourished; Qin employed punishment and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou employed benevolence and flourished; Qin employed punishment and perished.

sentences.zh: 願陛下緩刑用仁，天下幸甚！」

translations.literal: Your servant hopes Your Majesty will ease punishments and employ benevolence—the realm would be greatly blessed!"
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to ease punishments and employ benevolence—the realm would be greatly blessed!"

sentences.zh: 太后頗采其言，制獄稍衰。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager largely adopted his words, and prison regulations gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager largely adopted his words, and harsh prison practices gradually declined.

sentences.zh: 太后春秋雖高，善自塗澤，雖左右不覺其衰。

translations.literal: Although the Empress Dowager's years were advanced, she was skilled at applying cosmetics; even those at her side did not notice her decline.
translations.idiomatic: Although advanced in years, she was skilled at applying cosmetics; even those at her side did not notice her decline.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，敕以齒落更生，九月，庚子，御則天門，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: On bingxu an edict was issued that her teeth had fallen out and grown anew. In the ninth month, on gengzi, she proceeded to the Zetian Gate, proclaimed amnesty throughout the realm, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu an edict was issued that her teeth had fallen out and grown anew. In the ninth month, on gengzi, she proceeded to the Zetian Gate, proclaimed amnesty, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 更以九月為社。

translations.literal: The communal sacrifice was moved to the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: The communal sacrifice was moved to the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 制於并州置北都。

translations.literal: It was decreed that the Northern Capital be established at Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It was decreed that the Northern Capital be established at Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，同平章事李游道、王璿、袁智弘、崔神基、李元素、春官侍郎孔思元、益州長史任令輝，皆為王弘義所陷，流嶺南。

translations.literal: On guichou, Associate Directors Li Youdao, Wang Xuan, Yuan Zhihong, Cui Shenji, and Li Yuansu, Spring Office Vice Minister Kong Siyuan, and Senior Administrator of Yi Prefecture Ren Linghui—all were framed by Wang Hongyi and exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Associate Directors Li Youdao, Wang Xuan, Yuan Zhihong, Cui Shenji, and Li Yuansu, Spring Office Vice Minister Kong Siyuan, and Senior Administrator of Yi Prefecture Ren Linghui—all were framed by Wang Hongyi and exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 左羽林中郎將來子珣坐事流愛州，尋卒。

translations.literal: Central Army Lieutenant General Lai Zixun was exiled to Ai Prefecture for an offense and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Central Army Lieutenant General Lai Zixun was exiled to Ai Prefecture for an offense and soon died.

sentences.zh: 初，新豐王孝傑從劉審禮擊吐蕃，為副總管，與審禮皆沒於吐蕃。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince of Xinfeng Wang Xiaojie followed Liu Shenli in attacking the Tibetans as deputy commander; both he and Shenli were captured by the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince of Xinfeng Wang Xiaojie followed Liu Shenli in attacking the Tibetans as deputy commander; both were captured.

sentences.zh: 贊普見孝傑泣曰：「貌類吾父。」

translations.literal: The tsenpo saw Xiaojie and wept, saying, "Your appearance resembles my father."
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan ruler saw Xiaojie and wept, saying, "You look like my father."

sentences.zh: 厚禮之，後竟得歸，累遷右鷹揚衛將軍。

translations.literal: He treated him with generous courtesy; later Xiaojie was able to return and was repeatedly promoted to General of the Right Yingyang Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He treated him generously; later Xiaojie returned and rose to General of the Right Yingyang Guard.

sentences.zh: 孝傑久在吐蕃，知其虛實。

translations.literal: Xiaojie had long been among the Tibetans and knew their strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojie had long been among the Tibetans and knew their strengths and weaknesses.

sentences.zh: 會西州都督唐休璟請復取龜茲、于闐、疏勒、碎葉四鎮，敕以孝傑為武威軍總管，與左武衛大將軍阿史那忠節將兵擊吐蕃。

translations.literal: When Protector-General of Xi Prefecture Tang Xiujing requested recovery of the four garrisons of Kucha, Khotan, Kashgar, and Suyab, an edict appointed Xiaojie Commander of the Wuwei Army, and with Left Martial Guard General Ashina Zhongjie he led troops to strike the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: When Protector-General of Xi Prefecture Tang Xiujing requested recovery of the four garrisons of Kucha, Khotan, Kashgar, and Suyab, Xiaojie was appointed Commander of the Wuwei Army and, with Left Martial Guard General Ashina Zhongjie, led troops against the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙戌，大破吐蕃，復取四鎮，置安西都護府於龜茲，發兵戍之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingxu, they greatly defeated the Tibetans, recovered the four garrisons, established the Protectorate-General of Anxi at Kucha, and dispatched troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on bingxu, they routed the Tibetans, recovered the four garrisons, established the Protectorate-General of Anxi at Kucha, and garrisoned it.

sentences.zh: 正月，壬辰朔，太后享萬象神宮，以魏王承嗣為亞獻，梁王三思為終獻。

translations.literal: In the first month, on the renchen new moon, the Empress Dowager offered sacrifice at the Temple of Myriad Images, with Prince of Wei Chengsi as secondary offerer and Prince of Liang Sansi as final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, on the renchen new moon, the Empress Dowager offered sacrifice at the Temple of Myriad Images, with Prince of Wei Chengsi as secondary offerer and Prince of Liang Sansi as final offerer.

sentences.zh: 太后自製神宮樂，用舞者九百人。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager herself composed the temple music, employing nine hundred dancers.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager herself composed the temple music, employing nine hundred dancers.

sentences.zh: 戶婢團兒為太后所寵信，有憾於皇嗣，乃譖皇嗣妃劉氏、德妃竇氏為厭咒。

translations.literal: The household maid Tuan'er was favored and trusted by the Empress Dowager. Bearing a grudge against the Heir Apparent, she slandered the Heir Apparent's consort Lady Liu and Virtuous Consort Lady Dou as practicing curse magic.
translations.idiomatic: The household maid Tuan'er was favored by the Empress Dowager. Bearing a grudge against the Heir Apparent, she slandered his consort Lady Liu and Virtuous Consort Lady Dou as practicing curse magic.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，妃與德妃朝太后於嘉豫殿，既退，同時殺之，瘞於宮中，莫知所在。

translations.literal: On siji, the consort and Virtuous Consort attended the Empress Dowager at Jiayu Hall; after they withdrew, both were killed at once and buried within the palace—no one knew where.
translations.idiomatic: On siji, the consort and Virtuous Consort attended the Empress Dowager at Jiayu Hall; after they withdrew, both were killed and buried within the palace—no one knew where.

sentences.zh: 德妃，抗之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort was a great-granddaughter of Dou Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort was a great-granddaughter of Dou Kang.

sentences.zh: 皇嗣畏忤旨，不敢言，居太后前，容止自如。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent feared to offend her will and dared not speak; in the Empress Dowager's presence his bearing and manner were as usual.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent feared to offend her and dared not speak; in her presence his bearing was as usual.

sentences.zh: 團兒復欲害皇嗣，有言其情於太后者，太后乃殺團兒。

translations.literal: Tuan'er again wished to harm the Heir Apparent; when someone reported her intentions to the Empress Dowager, she had Tuan'er killed.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan'er again wished to harm the Heir Apparent; when someone reported her intentions, the Empress Dowager had her killed.

sentences.zh: 是時，告密者皆誘人奴婢告其主，以求功賞。

translations.literal: At this time informers all induced people's slaves and servants to accuse their masters, seeking merit rewards.
translations.idiomatic: At this time informers induced slaves and servants to accuse their masters, seeking rewards.

sentences.zh: 德妃父孝諶為潤州刺史，有奴妄為妖異以恐德妃母龐氏，龐氏懼，奴請夜祠禱解，因發其事。

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort's father Xiaoqin was Prefect of Run Prefecture. A slave falsely performed uncanny acts to frighten Virtuous Consort's mother Lady Pang. Lady Pang was afraid; the slave asked to perform night sacrifices to pray for release and thereby exposed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous Consort's father Xiaoqin was Prefect of Run Prefecture. A slave staged uncanny acts to frighten her mother Lady Pang. Lady Pang was afraid; the slave asked to perform night sacrifices to pray for release and thereby exposed the affair.

sentences.zh: 下監察御史龍門薛季昶按之，季昶誣奏，以為與德妃同祝詛，先涕泣不自勝，乃言曰：「龐氏所為，臣子所不忍道。」

translations.literal: The case was sent down to Attending Censor Xue Jichang of Longmen for investigation. Jichang submitted a false memorial claiming she had joined Virtuous Consort in curses and prayers. First he wept uncontrollably, then said, "What Lady Pang has done—a subject cannot bear to speak of it."
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Xue Jichang of Longmen investigated. He submitted a false memorial claiming she had joined Virtuous Consort in curses. First he wept uncontrollably, then said, "What Lady Pang has done—a subject cannot bear to speak of it."

sentences.zh: 太后擢季昶為給事中。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager promoted Jichang to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager promoted Jichang to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 龐氏當斬，其子希瑊詣侍御史徐有功訟冤，有功牒所司停刑，上奏論之，以為無罪；

translations.literal: Lady Pang was to be beheaded. Her son Xizhen went to Attendant Censor Xu Yougong to plead injustice. Yougong sent a dispatch to the relevant office to halt execution and memorialized arguing she was guiltless;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pang was to be beheaded. Her son Xizhen went to Attendant Censor Xu Yougong to plead injustice. Yougong ordered execution halted and memorialized that she was guiltless;

sentences.zh: 季昶奏有功阿黨惡逆，請付法，法司處有功罪當絞。

translations.literal: Jichang memorialized that Yougong had shielded a faction in grave treason and requested he be handed to the law; the legal office ruled Yougong's offense warranted strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Jichang memorialized that Yougong had shielded traitors and asked that he be handed to the law; the legal office ruled his offense warranted strangulation.

sentences.zh: 令史以白有功，有功歎曰：「豈我獨死，諸人永不死邪！」

translations.literal: A clerk reported this to Yougong. Yougong sighed and said, "Am I alone to die while others never die!"
translations.idiomatic: A clerk reported this to Yougong. Yougong sighed and said, "Am I alone to die while others never die!"

sentences.zh: 既食，掩扇而寢。

translations.literal: After eating, he drew the screen and slept.
translations.idiomatic: After eating, he drew the screen and slept.

sentences.zh: 人以為有功苟自強，必內憂懼，密伺之，方熟寢。

translations.literal: People thought Yougong was forcing himself to appear strong and must be inwardly fearful; they secretly watched him and found him sound asleep.
translations.idiomatic: People thought Yougong was forcing himself to appear strong and must be inwardly fearful; they secretly watched him and found him sound asleep.

sentences.zh: 太后召有功，迎謂曰：「卿比按獄，失出何多？」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager summoned Yougong and greeted him, saying, "In your recent examination of cases, how many wrongful releases have there been?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager summoned Yougong and asked, "In your recent examination of cases, how many wrongful releases have there been?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「失出，人臣之小過；

translations.literal: He replied, "Wrongful release is a minister's small fault;
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Wrongful release is a minister's small fault;

sentences.zh: 好生，聖人之大德。」

translations.literal: cherishing life is a sage's great virtue."
translations.idiomatic: cherishing life is a sage's great virtue."

sentences.zh: 太后默然。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was silent.

sentences.zh: 由是龐氏得減死，與其三子皆流嶺南，孝諶貶羅州司馬，有功亦除名。

translations.literal: Thereby Lady Pang's death was reduced; she and her three sons were all exiled to Lingnan. Xiaoqin was demoted to Military Assistant of Luo Prefecture, and Yougong was also removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby Lady Pang's death sentence was commuted; she and her three sons were exiled to Lingnan. Xiaoqin was demoted to Military Assistant of Luo Prefecture, and Yougong was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 戊申，姚璹奏請令宰相撰《時政記》，月送史館；

translations.literal: On wushen, Yao Shuo memorialized requesting that chancellors compile Records of Current Administration and send them monthly to the Historiography Office;
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Yao Shuo memorialized requesting that chancellors compile Records of Current Administration and send them monthly to the Historiography Office;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: this was approved.

sentences.zh: 《時政記》自此始。

translations.literal: Records of Current Administration began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Records of Current Administration began at this time.

sentences.zh: 臘月，丁卯，降皇孫成器為壽春王，恆王成義為衡陽王，楚王隆基為臨淄王，衛王隆范為巴陵王，趙王隆業為彭城王，皆睿宗之子也。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on dingmao, Imperial Grandson Chengq was demoted to Prince of Shouchun, Prince of Heng Chengyi to Prince of Hengyang, Prince of Chu Longji to Prince of Linzi, Prince of Wei Longfan to Prince of Baling, and Prince of Zhao Longye to Prince of Pengcheng—all sons of Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingmao, Imperial Grandson Chengq was demoted to Prince of Shouchun, Prince of Heng Chengyi to Prince of Hengyang, Prince of Chu Longji to Prince of Linzi, Prince of Wei Longfan to Prince of Baling, and Prince of Zhao Longye to Prince of Pengcheng—all sons of Ruizong.

sentences.zh: 春，一月，庚子，以夏官侍郎婁師德同平章事。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on gengzi, Summer Office Vice Minister Lou Shide was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on gengzi, Summer Office Vice Minister Lou Shide was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 師德寬厚清慎，犯而不校。

translations.literal: Shide was broad-minded, pure, and cautious; when offended he did not contend.
translations.idiomatic: Shide was broad-minded, pure, and cautious; when offended he did not contend.

sentences.zh: 與李昭德俱入朝，師德體肥行緩，昭德屢待之不至，怒罵曰：「田舍夫！」

translations.literal: Entering court together with Li Zhaode, Shide was stout and walked slowly. Zhaode repeatedly waited for him but he did not arrive and angrily cursed, "Country bumpkin!"
translations.idiomatic: Entering court with Li Zhaode, Shide was stout and walked slowly. Zhaode repeatedly waited for him in vain and angrily cursed, "Country bumpkin!"

sentences.zh: 師德徐笑曰：「師德不為田舍夫，誰當為之！」

translations.literal: Shide smiled slowly and said, "If Shide is not the country bumpkin, who should be!"
translations.idiomatic: Shide smiled and said, "If I am not the country bumpkin, who should be!"

sentences.zh: 其弟除代州刺史，將行，師德謂曰：「吾備位宰相，汝復為州牧，榮寵過盛，人所疾也，將何以自免？」

translations.literal: His younger brother was appointed Prefect of Dai Prefecture and was about to depart. Shide said to him, "I hold a chancellor's post in name only, and you again become a prefect—the honor is excessive and people resent it. How will you protect yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was appointed Prefect of Dai Prefecture and was about to depart. Shide said, "I hold a chancellor's post in name only, and you become a prefect—our honors are excessive and people resent it. How will you protect yourself?"

sentences.zh: 弟長跪曰：「自今雖有人唾某面，某拭之而已，庶不為兄憂。」

translations.literal: His brother knelt long and said, "From now on, even if someone spits in my face, I shall merely wipe it—perhaps my brother need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: His brother knelt and said, "From now on, even if someone spits in my face, I shall merely wipe it—perhaps you need not worry."

sentences.zh: 師德愀然曰：「此所以為吾憂也！

translations.literal: Shide said gravely, "This is exactly what worries me!
translations.idiomatic: Shide said gravely, "This is exactly what worries me!

sentences.zh: 人唾汝面，怒汝也；

translations.literal: When a man spits in your face, he is angry with you;
translations.idiomatic: When a man spits in your face, he is angry with you;

sentences.zh: 汝拭之，乃逆其意，所以重其怒。

translations.literal: if you wipe it, you go against his intent and thereby deepen his anger.
translations.idiomatic: if you wipe it, you go against his intent and deepen his anger.

sentences.zh: 夫唾，不拭自干，當笑而受之。」

translations.literal: Spittle, left unwiped, dries of itself—you should smile and accept it."
translations.idiomatic: Spittle, left unwiped, dries of itself—you should smile and accept it."

sentences.zh: 甲寅，前尚方監裴匪躬、內常侍范雲仙坐私謁皇嗣，腰斬於市。

translations.literal: On jiayin, former Director of the Palace Workshops Pei Feigong and Inner Regular Attendant Fan Yunxian were executed by waist severance in the market for privately visiting the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, former Director of the Palace Workshops Pei Feigong and Inner Regular Attendant Fan Yunxian were cut in two at the waist in the market for privately visiting the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 自是公卿以下皆不得見。

translations.literal: From this time none from the dukes and ministers downward were permitted to see him.
translations.idiomatic: From this time none from the dukes and ministers downward were permitted to see him.

sentences.zh: 又有告皇嗣潛有異謀者，太后命來俊臣鞫其左右，左右不勝楚毒，皆欲自誣。

translations.literal: Someone again reported that the Heir Apparent secretly harbored treacherous designs. The Empress Dowager ordered Lai Junchen to interrogate his attendants; unable to bear Chu torture, they all wished to falsely incriminate themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Someone again reported that the Heir Apparent secretly harbored treacherous designs. The Empress Dowager ordered Lai Junchen to interrogate his attendants; unable to bear torture, they all wished to falsely incriminate themselves.

sentences.zh: 太常工人京兆安金藏大呼謂俊臣曰：「公既不信金藏之言，請剖心以明皇嗣不反。」

translations.literal: An Jinzang, a worker of the Imperial Ancestral Temple from Jingzhao, shouted to Junchen, "Since you do not believe Jinzang's words, I beg to cut open my heart to show the Heir Apparent has not rebelled."
translations.idiomatic: An Jinzang, a worker of the Imperial Ancestral Temple from Jingzhao, shouted to Junchen, "Since you do not believe me, I beg to cut open my heart to show the Heir Apparent has not rebelled."

sentences.zh: 即引佩刀自剖其胸，五藏皆出，流血被地。

translations.literal: He immediately drew his belt knife and cut open his own breast; all five viscera came out and blood covered the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately drew his belt knife and cut open his breast; all five viscera came out and blood covered the ground.

sentences.zh: 太后聞之，令轝入宮中，使醫內五藏，以桑皮線縫之，傅以藥，經宿始蘇。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager heard of it, she ordered him carried into the palace, had physicians replace his five viscera, sew him with mulberry-bark thread, apply medicine, and only after one night did he revive.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager heard of it, she ordered him carried into the palace, had physicians replace his five viscera, sew him with mulberry-bark thread, apply medicine, and only after one night did he revive.

sentences.zh: 太后親臨視之，歎曰：「吾有子不能自明，使汝至此。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager came in person to see him and sighed, "I have a son who could not clear himself and brought you to this."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager came in person to see him and sighed, "I have a son who could not clear himself and brought you to this."

sentences.zh: 既命俊臣停推。

translations.literal: She then ordered Junchen to halt the investigation.
translations.idiomatic: She then ordered Junchen to halt the investigation.

sentences.zh: 睿宗由是得免。

translations.literal: Ruizong was thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong was thereby spared.

sentences.zh: 罷舉人習《老子》，更習太后所造《臣軌》。

translations.literal: The examination candidates' study of the 《Laozi》 was abolished, and they were made to study instead the 《Tracks of the Ministers》 composed by the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Study of the 《Laozi》 for examination candidates was abolished, and they were made to study instead the Empress Dowager's 《Tracks of the Ministers》.

sentences.zh: 二月，丙子，新羅王政明卒，遣使立其子理洪為王。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingzi, King Jeongmyeong of Silla died; envoys were sent to install his son Richung as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingzi, King Jeongmyeong of Silla died; envoys were sent to install his son Richung as king.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，禁人間錦。

translations.literal: On yihai, brocade among the populace was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, brocade among the populace was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 侍御史侯思止私畜錦，李照德按之，杖殺於朝堂。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Hou Sizhi privately hoarded brocade; Li Zhaode investigated him and had him beaten to death in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Hou Sizhi privately hoarded brocade; Li Zhaode investigated him and had him beaten to death in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 或告嶺南流人謀反，太后遣司刑評事萬國俊攝監察御史就按之。

translations.literal: Someone reported that exiles in Lingnan were plotting rebellion; the Empress Dowager sent Legal Officer of the Ministry of Justice Wan Guojun as acting investigating censor to investigate on site.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that exiles in Lingnan were plotting rebellion; the Empress Dowager sent Legal Officer Wan Guojun as acting investigating censor to investigate on site.

sentences.zh: 國俊至廣州，悉召流入，矯制賜自盡。

translations.literal: Guojun reached Guangzhou, summoned all exiles, and by forged edict granted them suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Guojun reached Guangzhou, summoned all exiles, and by forged edict ordered them to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 流人號呼不服，國俊驅就水曲，盡斬之，一朝殺三百餘人。

translations.literal: The exiles cried out in protest; Guojun drove them to the river bend and beheaded them all—in one morning more than three hundred were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The exiles cried out in protest; Guojun drove them to the river bend and beheaded them all—in one morning more than three hundred were killed.

sentences.zh: 然後詐為反狀，還奏，因言諸道流人，亦必有怨望謀反者，不可不早誅。

translations.literal: He then forged evidence of rebellion and returned to memorialize, saying that exiles in every circuit surely also harbored resentment and treasonous designs and could not but be executed early.
translations.idiomatic: He then forged evidence of rebellion and returned to memorialize, saying that exiles in every circuit surely also harbored resentment and treasonous designs and must be executed without delay.

sentences.zh: 太后喜，擢國俊為朝散大夫、行侍御史。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was pleased and promoted Guojun to Gentleman for Dispersing the Court and acting investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was pleased and promoted Guojun to Gentleman for Dispersing the Court and acting investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 更遣右翊衛兵曹參軍劉光業、司刑評事王德壽、苑南面監丞鮑思恭、尚輦直長王大貞、右武威衛兵曹參軍屈貞筠皆攝監察御史，詣諸道按流人。

translations.literal: She further sent Right Assistant Guard Army Registrar Liu Guangye, Legal Officer Wang Deshou, Southern Park of the Imperial Garden Supervisor Bao Sigong, Imperial Transport Chief Clerk Wang Dazhen, and Right Mighty Martial Guard Army Registrar Qu Zhenyun, all as acting investigating censors, to investigate exiles in the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: She further sent Liu Guangye, Wang Deshou, Bao Sigong, Wang Dazhen, and Qu Zhenyun, all as acting investigating censors, to investigate exiles in the various circuits.

sentences.zh: 光業等以國俊多殺蒙賞，爭效之，光業殺七百人，德壽殺五百人，自餘少者不減百人，其遠年雜犯流人亦與之俱斃。

translations.literal: Guangye and the others, seeing that Guojun had been rewarded for mass killing, vied to imitate him—Guangye killed seven hundred, Deshou five hundred, and the rest no fewer than a hundred each; even exiles sent long before for miscellaneous offenses were killed along with them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangye and the others, seeing that Guojun had been rewarded for mass killing, vied to imitate him—Guangye killed seven hundred, Deshou five hundred, and the rest no fewer than a hundred each; even exiles sent long before for miscellaneous offenses were killed along with them.

sentences.zh: 太后頗知其濫，制：「六道流人未死者並家屬皆聽還鄉里。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager learned rather fully of the excess and decreed: "Exiles in the six circuits who have not yet died, together with their families, are all permitted to return to their home districts."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager learned of the excess and decreed: "Exiles in the six circuits who have not yet died, together with their families, are all permitted to return home."

sentences.zh: 國俊等亦相繼死，或得罪流竄。

translations.literal: Guojun and the others also died one after another, or were found guilty and exiled.
translations.idiomatic: Guojun and the others also died one after another, or were found guilty and exiled.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣誣冬官尚書蘇干，雲在魏州與琅邪王沖通謀，夏，四月，乙未，殺之。

translations.literal: Lai Junchen falsely charged Minister of the Winter Office Su Gan, saying he had conspired with Prince Langye Chong at Weizhou; in summer, the fourth month, on yiwei, Gan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen falsely charged Minister of the Winter Office Su Gan with conspiring with Prince Langye Chong at Weizhou; in summer, the fourth month, on yiwei, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸丑，棣州河溢，流二千餘家。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on guichou, the river at Dizhou overflowed and swept away more than two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guichou, the river at Dizhou overflowed and swept away more than two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，丁亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, on the dinghai new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, on the dinghai new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 魏王承嗣等五千人表請加尊號曰金輪聖神皇帝。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Chengsi and others, five thousand in all, memorialized requesting that the honorific title Golden Wheel Sage Spirit Emperor be added.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Chengsi and others, five thousand in all, memorialized requesting the honorific title Golden Wheel Sage Spirit Emperor.

sentences.zh: 乙未，太后御衛象神宮，受尊號，赦天下。

translations.literal: On yiwei, the Empress Dowager proceeded to the Weixiang Spirit Palace, received the honorific, and proclaimed an amnesty throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, the Empress Dowager proceeded to the Weixiang Spirit Palace, received the honorific, and proclaimed an amnesty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 作金輪等七寶，每朝會，陳之殿庭。

translations.literal: She had the seven treasures including the Golden Wheel made, and at every court assembly they were displayed in the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: She had the seven treasures including the Golden Wheel made, and at every court assembly they were displayed in the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 庚子，追尊昭安皇帝曰渾元昭安皇帝，文穆皇帝曰立極文穆皇帝，孝明高皇帝曰無上孝明高皇帝，皇后從帝號。

translations.literal: On gengzi, posthumous honors were raised: Emperor Zhao'an was titled Hunyuan Zhao'an Emperor, Emperor Wenmu was titled Liji Wenmu Emperor, Emperor Xiaoming Gao was titled Supreme Xiaoming Gao Emperor, and the empresses followed their emperors' titles.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, posthumous honors were raised: Emperor Zhao'an was titled Hunyuan Zhao'an Emperor, Emperor Wenmu was titled Liji Wenmu Emperor, Emperor Xiaoming Gao was titled Supreme Xiaoming Gao Emperor, and the empresses took titles matching their emperors.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以文昌左丞、同平章事姚璹為司賓卿，罷政事；

translations.literal: On xinchou, Yao Shuo, Associate Director of the Chancellery and Minister of the Left at Wenchang, was made Minister of Guests for Foreign Embassies and removed from the chancellery;
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Yao Shuo, Associate Director of the Chancellery and Minister of the Left at Wenchang, was made Minister of Guests and removed from the chancellery;

sentences.zh: 以司賓卿萬年豆盧欽望為內史，文昌左丞韋巨源同平章事，秋官侍郎吳人陸元方為鸞台侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Doulu Qinwang of Wannian, formerly Minister of Guests, was made Chief Secretary; Minister of the Left at Wenchang Wei Juyuan was made Associate Director of the Chancellery; Wu native Lu Yuanfang, Vice Minister of the Autumn Office, was made Vice Minister at Fengge and Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Doulu Qinwang of Wannian, formerly Minister of Guests, was made Chief Secretary; Wei Juyuan, Minister of the Left at Wenchang, was made Associate Director of the Chancellery; Lu Yuanfang of Wu, Vice Minister of the Autumn Office, was made Vice Minister at Fengge and Associate Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 巨源，孝寬之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Juyuan was the great-great-grandson of Wei Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan was the great-great-grandson of Wei Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 正月，丙戌，太后享萬象神宮。

translations.literal: In the first month, on bingxu, the Empress Dowager sacrificed at the Spirit Palace of Myriad Images.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, on bingxu, the Empress Dowager sacrificed at the Spirit Palace of Myriad Images.

sentences.zh: 突厥可汗骨篤祿卒，其子幼，弟默啜自立為可汗。

translations.literal: Gudulu, qaghan of the Turks, died; his son was young, and his younger brother Mochuo installed himself as qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Gudulu, qaghan of the Turks, died; his son was young, and his younger brother Mochuo installed himself as qaghan.

sentences.zh: 臘月，甲戌，默啜寇靈州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiaxu, Mochuo raided Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiaxu, Mochuo raided Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 室韋反，遣右鷹揚衛大將軍李多祚擊破之。

translations.literal: The Shiwei rebelled; Right General of the Hawk-raising Guard Li Duozuo was sent and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiwei rebelled; Right General of the Hawk-raising Guard Li Duozuo was sent and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 春，一月，以婁師德為河源等軍檢校營田大使。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Lou Shide was made Commissioner for Inspecting Army Farms of the Heyuan and other armies.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Lou Shide was made Commissioner for Inspecting Army Farms of the Heyuan and other armies.

sentences.zh: 二月，武威道總管王孝傑破吐蕃孛文論贊刃、突厥可汗俀子等於泠泉及大嶺，各三萬餘人，碎葉鎮守使韓思忠破泥熟俟斤等萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the second month, Regional Commander Wang Xiaojie of the Wuwei Circuit defeated the Tibetan Lun Wenlun Zanren and the Turkish qaghan's son Erzi and others at Lengquan and Dalin, more than thirty thousand each; Defender of Suyab Han Sizhong defeated the Nishuobi qaghan and others, more than ten thousand.
