translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Wang Xiaojie, regional commander of the Wuwei Circuit, defeated the Tibetans Lun Wenlun Zanren and the Turkish qaghan's son Erzi and others at Lengquan and Dalin, more than thirty thousand each; Han Sizhong, defender of Suyab, defeated the Nishuobi qaghan and others, more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以僧懷義為代北道行軍大總管，以討默啜。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the monk Huaiyi was made Grand Commander of the Daibei Circuit Field Army to attack Mochuo.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the monk Huaiyi was made Grand Commander of the Daibei Circuit Field Army to attack Mochuo.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲申，以鳳閣舍人蘇味道為鳳閣侍郎、同平章事，李昭德檢校內史，更以僧懷義為朔方道行軍大總管，以李昭德為長史，蘇味道為司馬，帥契苾明、曹仁師、沙吒忠義等十八將軍以討默啜，未行，虜退而止。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiashen, Fengge Attendant Su Weidao was made Vice Minister at Fengge and Associate Director of the Chancellery; Li Zhaode was made acting Chief Secretary; the monk Huaiyi was again made Grand Commander of the Shuofang Circuit Field Army, with Li Zhaode as chief administrator and Su Weidao as vice administrator, leading Qibi Ming, Cao Renshi, Shazha Zhongyi, and eighteen other generals to attack Mochuo—but before they marched, the barbarians withdrew and the campaign was halted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiashen, Su Weidao was made Vice Minister at Fengge and Associate Director of the Chancellery; Li Zhaode was made acting Chief Secretary; Huaiyi was again made Grand Commander of the Shuofang Circuit Field Army, with Li Zhaode as chief administrator and Su Weidao as vice administrator, leading Qibi Ming, Cao Renshi, Shazha Zhongyi, and eighteen other generals against Mochuo—but before they marched, the barbarians withdrew and the campaign was called off.

sentences.zh: 昭德嘗與懷義議事，失其旨，懷義撻之，昭德惶懼請罪。

translations.literal: Zhaode once discussed affairs with Huaiyi, missed his intent, and Huaiyi flogged him; Zhaode in fear begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode once discussed affairs with Huaiyi, missed his intent, and Huaiyi flogged him; Zhaode fearfully begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬戌，以夏官尚書、武威道大總管王孝傑同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on renxu, Summer Office Minister and Grand Commander of the Wuwei Circuit Wang Xiaojie was made a third-rank official of Fengge and Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on renxu, Summer Office Minister and Grand Commander of the Wuwei Circuit Wang Xiaojie was made a third-rank official of Fengge and Luantai.

sentences.zh: 五月，魏王承嗣等二萬六千餘人上尊號曰越古金輪聖神皇帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Prince of Wei Chengsi and more than twenty-six thousand others offered the honorific title Transcending Antiquity Golden Wheel Sage Spirit Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Prince of Wei Chengsi and more than twenty-six thousand others offered the honorific title Transcending Antiquity Golden Wheel Sage Spirit Emperor.

sentences.zh: 甲午，御則天門樓受尊號，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: On jiawu, she proceeded to the Zetian Gate tower to receive the honorific, proclaimed an amnesty throughout the realm, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, she proceeded to the Zetian Gate tower to receive the honorific, proclaimed an amnesty, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 天授中，遣監察御史壽春裴懷古安集西南蠻。

translations.literal: During the Tianshou era, Investigating Censor Pei Huaigu of Shouchun was sent to pacify and settle the southwestern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era, Investigating Censor Pei Huaigu of Shouchun was sent to pacify the southwestern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸丑，永昌蠻酋薰期帥部落二十餘萬戶內附。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guichou, Xunqi, chieftain of the Yongchang barbarians, led more than two hundred thousand households of his tribes to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guichou, Xunqi, chieftain of the Yongchang barbarians, led more than two hundred thousand households of his tribes to submit.

sentences.zh: 河內有老尼居神都麟趾寺，與嵩山人韋什方等以妖妄惑眾。

translations.literal: In Henei, an old nun dwelling at Linzhi Temple in Shendu, together with Wei Shifang of Mount Song and others, deluded the masses with sorcery and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: In Henei, an old nun at Linzhi Temple in Shendu, together with Wei Shifang of Mount Song and others, deluded the masses with sorcery and falsehood.

sentences.zh: 尼自號淨光如來，雲能知未然；

translations.literal: The nun styled herself the Tathāgata of Pure Light and claimed she could know what had not yet happened;
translations.idiomatic: The nun styled herself the Tathāgata of Pure Light and claimed she could know the future;

sentences.zh: 什方自雲吳赤烏元年生。

translations.literal: Shifang claimed he was born in the first year of Chiwu under Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Shifang claimed he was born in the first year of Chiwu under Wu.

sentences.zh: 又有老胡亦自言五百歲，雲見薛師已二百年矣，容貌愈少。

translations.literal: There was also an old barbarian who claimed to be five hundred years old and said he had seen Xue Huaiyi two hundred years ago, yet looked ever younger.
translations.idiomatic: There was also an old barbarian who claimed to be five hundred years old and said he had seen Xue Huaiyi two hundred years before, yet looked ever younger.

sentences.zh: 太后甚信重之，賜什方姓武氏。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager greatly trusted and favored them and granted Shifang the surname Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager greatly trusted and favored them and granted Shifang the surname Wu.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸未，以什方為正諫大夫、同平章事，制云：「邁軒代之廣成，逾漢朝之河上。」

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guiwei, Shifang was made Rectifier Remonstrant and Associate Director of the Chancellery; the edict said, "Surpassing Guangcheng of the Xuanyuan age, exceeding the Riverbank Master of the Han dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on guiwei, Shifang was made Rectifier Remonstrant and Associate Director of the Chancellery; the edict said, "Surpassing Guangcheng of the Xuanyuan age, exceeding the Riverbank Master of the Han dynasty."

sentences.zh: 八月，什方乞還山，制罷遣之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Shifang begged to return to the mountains, and by edict he was dismissed and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Shifang begged to return to the mountains, and by edict he was dismissed and sent away.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以王孝傑為瀚海道行軍總管，仍受朔方道行軍大總管薛懷義節度。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Wang Xiaojie was made Commander of the Hanhai Circuit Field Army and still placed under the command of Grand Commander of the Shuofang Circuit Field Army Xue Huaiyi.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Wang Xiaojie was made Commander of the Hanhai Circuit Field Army and still placed under the command of Grand Commander Xue Huaiyi of the Shuofang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以司賓少卿姚璹為納言；

translations.literal: On jisi, Vice Minister of Guests Yao Shuo was made Chief Remonstrator;
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Vice Minister of Guests Yao Shuo was made Chief Remonstrator;

sentences.zh: 左肅政中丞原武楊再思為鸞台侍郎，洛州司馬杜景儉為鳳閣侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: Yang Zaisi of Yuanwu, Left Censor-in-Chief, was made Luantai Vice Minister; Du Jingjian of Luozhou, Vice Military Commissioner, was made Fengge Vice Minister—all Associate Directors of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaisi of Yuanwu, Left Censor-in-Chief, was made Luantai Vice Minister; Du Jingjian of Luozhou, Vice Military Commissioner, was made Fengge Vice Minister—all were made Associate Directors of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 豆盧欽望請京官九品已上輸兩月俸以贍軍，轉帖百官，令拜表。

translations.literal: Doulu Qinwang requested that capital officials of the ninth rank and above contribute two months' salary to support the army, circulated a notice among all officials, and ordered them to submit memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Doulu Qinwang requested that capital officials of the ninth rank and above contribute two months' salary to support the army, circulated a notice among all officials, and ordered them to submit memorials.

sentences.zh: 百官但赴拜，不知何事。

translations.literal: The officials all came to pay respects but did not know what it was for.
translations.idiomatic: The officials all came to pay respects but did not know what it was for.

sentences.zh: 拾遺王求禮謂欽望曰：「明公祿厚，輸之無傷；

translations.literal: Remonstrator Wang Qiuli said to Qinwang, "Your Grace's salary is ample—contributing would do no harm;
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrator Wang Qiuli said to Qinwang, "Your Grace's salary is ample—contributing would do no harm;

sentences.zh: 卑官貧迫，奈何不使其知而欺奪之乎？」

translations.literal: low officials are poor and pressed—how can you not let them know and seize from them by deception?"
translations.idiomatic: low officials are poor and pressed—how can you not let them know and seize from them by deception?"

sentences.zh: 欽望正色拒之。

translations.literal: Qinwang sternly refused him.
translations.idiomatic: Qinwang sternly refused him.

sentences.zh: 既上表，求禮進言曰：「陛下富有四海，軍國有儲，何藉貧官九品之俸而欺奪之！」

translations.literal: After the memorial was submitted, Qiuli advanced and said, "Your Majesty possesses all within the four seas; the state and army have stores—why rely on seizing the salaries of poor ninth-rank officials by deception!"
translations.idiomatic: After the memorial was submitted, Qiuli advanced and said, "Your Majesty possesses all within the four seas; the state and army have stores—why rely on seizing the salaries of poor ninth-rank officials by deception!"

sentences.zh: 姚璹曰：「求禮不識大體。」

translations.literal: Yao Shuo said, "Qiuli does not understand the larger interest."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuo said, "Qiuli does not understand the larger interest."

sentences.zh: 求禮曰：「如姚璹，為識大體者邪？」

translations.literal: Qiuli said, "As for Yao Shuo—is he one who understands the larger interest?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli said, "As for Yao Shuo—is he one who understands the larger interest?"

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was thereupon dropped.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，鸞台侍郎、同平章事崔元綜坐事流振州。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Luantai Vice Minister and Associate Director Cui Yuanzong was banished to Zhenzhou on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Luantai Vice Minister and Associate Director Cui Yuanzong was banished to Zhenzhou on account of an offense.

sentences.zh: 武三思帥四夷酋長請鑄銅鐵為天樞，立於端門之外，銘紀功德，黜唐頌周；

translations.literal: Wu Sansi led chieftains of the four barbarians to request casting bronze and iron into a Sky Pillar, erecting it outside the Duan Gate, inscribing meritorious deeds, denouncing Tang and praising Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi led chieftains of the four barbarians to request casting bronze and iron into a Sky Pillar, erecting it outside the Duan Gate, inscribing meritorious deeds, denouncing Tang and praising Zhou;

sentences.zh: 以姚璹為督作使。

translations.literal: Yao Shuo was made superintendent of construction.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuo was made superintendent of construction.

sentences.zh: 諸胡聚錢百萬億，買銅鐵不能足，賦民間農器以足之。

translations.literal: The various barbarians collected money by the hundred million, yet could not buy enough bronze and iron; farm tools among the populace were levied to make up the shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: The various barbarians collected money by the hundred million, yet could not buy enough bronze and iron; farm tools among the populace were levied to make up the shortfall.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the renwu new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the renwu new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 殿中丞來俊臣坐贓貶同州參軍。

translations.literal: Palace Aide Lai Junchen was demoted to Army Registrar of Tongzhou on a charge of corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Aide Lai Junchen was demoted to Army Registrar of Tongzhou on a charge of corruption.

sentences.zh: 王弘義流瓊州，詐稱敕追還，至漢北，侍御史胡元禮遇之，按驗，得其奸狀，杖殺之。

translations.literal: Wang Hongyi was exiled to Qiongzhou, falsely claimed an edict summoning him back, and when he reached north of the Han River, Investigating Censor Hu Yuanli encountered him, investigated, obtained proof of his fraud, and had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongyi was exiled to Qiongzhou, falsely claimed an edict summoning him back, and when he reached north of the Han River, Investigating Censor Hu Yuanli encountered him, investigated, obtained proof of his fraud, and had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 內史李昭德恃太后委遇，頗專權使氣，人多疾之。

translations.literal: Chief Secretary Li Zhaode, relying on the Empress Dowager's trust and favor, was quite domineering and overbearing; many resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Secretary Li Zhaode, relying on the Empress Dowager's trust, was domineering and overbearing; many resented him.

sentences.zh: 前魯王府功曹參軍丘愔上疏攻之，其略曰：「陛下天授以前，萬機獨斷。

translations.literal: Former Army Adjutant of the Prince of Lu's household Qiu Yin submitted a memorial attacking him; the gist said, "Before the Tianshou era, Your Majesty alone decided all affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Former Army Adjutant of the Prince of Lu's household Qiu Yin submitted a memorial attacking him; the gist said, "Before the Tianshou era, Your Majesty alone decided all affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 自長壽以來，委任昭德，參奉機密，獻可替否；

translations.literal: Since the Changshou era, you have entrusted Zhaode, who participates in confidential matters and offers approval or rejection;
translations.idiomatic: Since the Changshou era, you have entrusted Zhaode, who participates in confidential matters and offers approval or rejection;

sentences.zh: 事有便利，不預咨謀，要待畫日將行，方乃別生駁異。

translations.literal: when a matter is advantageous, he does not consult beforehand; he waits until the day is marked for execution, then raises separate objections.
translations.idiomatic: when a matter is advantageous, he does not consult beforehand; he waits until the day is marked for execution, then raises separate objections.

sentences.zh: 揚露專擅，顯示於人，歸美引愆，義不如此。」

translations.literal: He displays his monopoly of power before others; to attribute merit and shift blame in this way is not proper."
translations.idiomatic: He displays his monopoly of power before others; to attribute merit and shift blame in this way is not proper."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「臣觀其膽，乃大於身，鼻息所沖，上拂雲漢。」

translations.literal: He also said, "Your servant observes that his gall is larger than his body; the breath from his nostrils strikes upward to the clouds."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "I observe that his gall is larger than his body; the breath from his nostrils strikes upward to the clouds."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「蟻穴壞堤，針芒寫氣，權重一去，收之極難。」

translations.literal: He also said, "An ant hole ruins a dike; a needle tip vents vital energy—once heavy authority is lost, recovering it is extremely difficult."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "An ant hole ruins a dike; a needle tip vents vital energy—once heavy authority is lost, recovering it is extremely difficult."

sentences.zh: 長上果毅鄧注，又著《石論》數千言，述昭德專權之狀。

translations.literal: Deng Zhu, a senior guardsman of the Long Service, also wrote the 《Treatise on Stone》, several thousand words in length, describing Zhaode's monopoly of power.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Zhu, a senior guardsman of the Long Service, also wrote the 《Treatise on Stone》, several thousand words in length, describing Zhaode's monopoly of power.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣舍人逄弘敏取奏之，太后由是惡昭德。

translations.literal: Fengge Attendant Pang Hongmin took it and submitted it; the Empress Dowager thereby came to dislike Zhaode.
translations.idiomatic: Fengge Attendant Pang Hongmin took it and submitted it; the Empress Dowager thereby came to dislike Zhaode.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，貶昭德為南賓尉，尋又免死流竄。

translations.literal: On renyin, Zhaode was demoted to Military Assistant of Nanbin; soon afterward he was spared death but exiled.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Zhaode was demoted to Military Assistant of Nanbin; soon afterward he was spared death but exiled.

sentences.zh: 太后出梨花一枝以示宰相，宰相皆以為瑞。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager brought out a spray of pear blossom to show the chancellors; the chancellors all regarded it as an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager brought out a spray of pear blossom to show the chancellors; the chancellors all regarded it as an auspicious sign.

sentences.zh: 杜景儉獨曰：「今草木黃落，而此更發榮，陰陽不時，咎在臣等。」

translations.literal: Du Jingjian alone said, "Now the grasses and trees are yellowing and falling, yet this flourishes anew—the yin and yang are untimely; the fault lies with us ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Du Jingjian alone said, "Now the grasses and trees are yellowing and falling, yet this flourishes anew—the yin and yang are untimely; the fault lies with us ministers."

sentences.zh: 因拜謝。

translations.literal: He thereupon bowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon bowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「卿真宰相也！」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "You are a true chancellor!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "You are a true chancellor!"

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬申，以文昌右丞李元素為鳳閣侍郎，右肅政中丞周允元檢校鳳閣侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renshen, Minister of the Right at Wenchang Li Yuansu was made Fengge Vice Minister, and Right Censor-in-Chief Zhou Yun'yuan was made acting Fengge Vice Minister—both Associate Directors of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on renshen, Li Yuansu, Minister of the Right at Wenchang, was made Fengge Vice Minister, and Zhou Yun'yuan, Right Censor-in-Chief, was made acting Fengge Vice Minister—both Associate Directors of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 允元，豫州人也。

translations.literal: Yun'yuan was a native of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yun'yuan was a native of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嶺南獠反，以容州都督張玄遇為桂、永等州經略大使以討之。

translations.literal: The Liao barbarians of Lingnan rebelled; Zhang Xuanyu, military governor of Rongzhou, was made Grand Coordinator for Gui, Yong, and other prefectures to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao barbarians of Lingnan rebelled; Zhang Xuanyu, military governor of Rongzhou, was made Grand Coordinator for Gui, Yong, and other prefectures to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 正月，辛巳朔，太后加號慈氏越古金輪聖神皇帝，赦天下，改元證聖。

translations.literal: In the first month, on the xinsi new moon, the Empress Dowager added the title Cishi Transcending Antiquity Golden Wheel Sage Spirit Emperor, proclaimed an amnesty throughout the realm, and changed the era name to Zhengsheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month, on the xinsi new moon, the Empress Dowager added the title Cishi Transcending Antiquity Golden Wheel Sage Spirit Emperor, proclaimed an amnesty, and changed the era name to Zhengsheng.

sentences.zh: 周允元與司刑少卿皇甫文備奏內史豆盧欽望、同平章事韋巨源、杜景儉、蘇味道、陸元方附會李昭德，不能匡正，欽望貶趙州，巨源貶麟州，景儉貶溱州，味道貶集州，元方貶綏州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhou Yun'yuan and Vice Minister of Justice Huangfu Wenbei memorialized that Chief Secretary Doulu Qinwang and Associate Directors Wei Juyuan, Du Jingjian, Su Weidao, and Lu Yuanfang had sided with Li Zhaode and failed to correct him—Qinwang was demoted to Zhaozhou, Juyuan to Linzhou, Jingjian to Qinzhou, Weidao to Jizhou, and Yuanfang to military governor of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yun'yuan and Vice Minister of Justice Huangfu Wenbei memorialized that Doulu Qinwang, Wei Juyuan, Du Jingjian, Su Weidao, and Lu Yuanfang had sided with Li Zhaode and failed to correct him—Qinwang was demoted to Zhaozhou, Juyuan to Linzhou, Jingjian to Qinzhou, Weidao to Jizhou, and Yuanfang to military governor of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，明堂既成，太后命僧懷義作夾紵大像，其小指中猶容數十人，於明堂北構天堂以貯之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Bright Hall was completed, the Empress Dowager ordered the monk Huaiyi to make a kapok-stuffed colossal image; its little finger could still hold several dozen people, and north of the Bright Hall she built the Hall of Heaven to store it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Bright Hall was completed, the Empress Dowager ordered the monk Huaiyi to make a kapok-stuffed colossal image; its little finger could still hold several dozen people, and north of the Bright Hall she built the Hall of Heaven to store it.

sentences.zh: 堂始構，為風所摧，更構之，日役萬人，采木江嶺，數年之間，所費以萬億計，府藏為之耗竭。

translations.literal: When construction of the hall first began, it was destroyed by wind; it was built again, with ten thousand men laboring daily; timber was gathered from the Yangzi valleys and mountain ranges—for several years the cost ran to hundreds of millions, and the treasury was drained.
translations.idiomatic: When construction first began, the hall was destroyed by wind; it was built again, with ten thousand men laboring daily; timber was gathered from the Yangzi valleys and mountain ranges—for several years the cost ran to hundreds of millions, and the treasury was drained.

sentences.zh: 懷義用財如糞土，太后一聽之，無所問。

translations.literal: Huaiyi spent wealth like dung; the Empress Dowager let him do as he pleased and asked nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi spent wealth like dung; the Empress Dowager let him do as he pleased and asked nothing.

sentences.zh: 每作無遮會，用錢萬緡；

translations.literal: Whenever he held an unhindered almsgiving assembly, he spent ten thousand strings of cash;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he held an unhindered almsgiving assembly, he spent ten thousand strings of cash;

sentences.zh: 士女雲集，又散錢十車，使之爭拾，相蹈踐有死者。

translations.literal: men and women gathered like clouds, and he also scattered ten cartloads of cash for them to scramble for; some were trampled to death.
translations.idiomatic: men and women gathered in crowds, and he also scattered ten cartloads of cash for them to scramble for; some were trampled to death.

sentences.zh: 所在公私田宅，多為僧有。

translations.literal: Public and private houses and fields everywhere came largely into the monks' possession.
translations.idiomatic: Public and private houses and fields everywhere came largely into the monks' possession.

sentences.zh: 懷義頗厭入宮，多居白馬寺，所度力士為僧者滿千人。

translations.literal: Huaiyi grew quite weary of entering the palace and mostly stayed at White Horse Temple; the strongmen he ordained as monks numbered a full thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiyi grew weary of entering the palace and mostly stayed at White Horse Temple; the strongmen he ordained as monks numbered a full thousand.

sentences.zh: 侍御史周矩疑有奸謀，固請按之。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Zhou Ju suspected a treacherous plot and firmly requested an investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Zhou Ju suspected a treacherous plot and firmly requested an investigation.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「卿姑退，朕即令往。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said, "Withdraw for now—I shall send you shortly."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Withdraw for now—I shall send you shortly."

sentences.zh: 矩至台，懷義亦至，乘馬就階而下，坦腹於床。

translations.literal: When Ju reached the censorate, Huaiyi also arrived, rode his horse down the steps, and lay bare-bellied on the couch.
translations.idiomatic: When Ju reached the censorate, Huaiyi also arrived, rode his horse down the steps, and lay bare-bellied on the couch.

sentences.zh: 矩召吏將按之，遽躍馬而去。

translations.literal: Ju summoned clerks to investigate him, but Huaiyi suddenly leaped on his horse and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ju summoned clerks to investigate him, but Huaiyi suddenly leaped on his horse and fled.

sentences.zh: 矩具奏其狀，太后曰：「此道人病風，不足詰，所度僧，惟卿所處。」

translations.literal: Ju fully memorialized the circumstances; the Empress Dowager said, "This man of the Way has wind sickness—nothing to question; as for the monks he ordained, deal with them as you see fit."
translations.idiomatic: Ju fully memorialized the circumstances; the Empress Dowager said, "This monk has wind sickness—nothing to question; as for the monks he ordained, deal with them as you see fit."

sentences.zh: 悉流遠州。

translations.literal: All were exiled to distant prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: All were exiled to distant prefectures.

sentences.zh: 遷矩天官員外郎。

translations.literal: Ju was transferred to be Outside Section Member at the Office of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was promoted to Outside Section Member at the Office of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 乙未，作無遮會於朝堂，鑿地為坑，深五丈，結綵為宮殿，佛像皆於坑中引出之，雲自地湧出。

translations.literal: On yiwei, an unhindered almsgiving assembly was held in the court hall; the ground was excavated into a pit five zhang deep, silk was woven into palaces, and Buddha images were all drawn up from within the pit, it being said that they surged forth from the earth.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Huaiyi held an unhindered almsgiving assembly in the court hall. Workers dug a pit five zhang deep, draped silk to form palaces, and hauled Buddha images up from the pit while claiming they were surging from the ground.

sentences.zh: 又殺牛取血，畫大像，首高二百尺，雲懷義刺膝血為之。

translations.literal: Cattle were again slaughtered for blood with which to paint a great image, its head two hundred chi high; it was said that Huaiyi had pricked his knee and used the blood for it.
translations.idiomatic: They slaughtered cattle for blood and painted a colossal image two hundred chi high at the head, claiming Huaiyi had drawn the blood from his own knee to make it.

sentences.zh: 丙申，張像於天津橋南，設齋。

translations.literal: On bingshen, the image was displayed south of the Tianjin Bridge and a vegetarian feast was set out.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, the image was erected south of the Tianjin Bridge and a ritual feast was held.

sentences.zh: 時御醫沈南□翏亦得幸於太后，懷義心慍，是夕，密燒天堂，延及明堂。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial physician Shen Nanqiu also won favor with the Empress Dowager; Huaiyi was resentful at heart, and that night secretly set fire to the Hall of Heaven, which spread to the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial physician Shen Nanqiu had also won the Empress Dowager's favor, and Huaiyi burned with jealousy. That night he secretly torched the Hall of Heaven, and the flames spread to the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 火照城中如晝，比明皆盡，暴風裂血像為數百段。

translations.literal: The fire lit the city as if it were day; by dawn all was consumed, and a violent wind tore the blood-painted image into several hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: The blaze lit the capital bright as noon. By dawn both halls were ashes, and a sudden gale shredded the blood-painted image into hundreds of fragments.

sentences.zh: 太后恥而諱之，但雲內作工徒誤燒麻主，遂涉明堂。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was shamed and concealed it, saying only that palace workmen had mistakenly burned the Mazhu shrine, which then involved the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, the Empress Dowager hushed the truth and announced only that construction workers had accidentally burned the Mazhu shrine, after which the fire reached the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 時方酺宴，左拾遺劉承慶請輟朝停酺以答天譴，太后將從之。

translations.literal: A grand feast was then in progress; Left Reminder Liu Chengqing requested that court be suspended and the feast halted to answer Heaven's reproof, and the Empress Dowager was about to consent.
translations.idiomatic: A grand feast was underway when Left Reminder Liu Chengqing urged the court to suspend audiences and cancel the revels as a response to Heaven's warning. The Empress Dowager was inclined to agree.

sentences.zh: 姚璹曰：「昔成周宣榭，卜代愈隆；

translations.literal: Yao Shuang said, "Of old, when the Xuanye terrace of accomplished Zhou burned, divination showed the succession would grow ever more glorious;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuang said, "When the Xuanye terrace of the Zhou burned, divination foretold a succession more glorious still;

sentences.zh: 漢武建章，盛德彌永。

translations.literal: when Emperor Wu of Han's Jianzhang Palace burned, sagely virtue endured the more.
translations.idiomatic: when Emperor Wu's Jianzhang Palace burned, his sagely virtue endured all the longer.

sentences.zh: 今明堂布政之所，非宗廟也，不應自貶損。」

translations.literal: The Bright Hall today is where government is proclaimed—not the ancestral temple; Your Majesty should not humble herself."
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall is where you govern, not where you worship your ancestors. You should not diminish yourself."

sentences.zh: 太后乃御端門，觀酺如平日。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager then took the Vermilion Gate and watched the feast as on ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager took her seat at the Vermilion Gate and watched the feast as though nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 命更造明堂、天堂，仍以懷義充使。

translations.literal: She ordered the Bright Hall and Hall of Heaven rebuilt and again appointed Huaiyi commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered the Bright Hall and Hall of Heaven rebuilt and again put Huaiyi in charge of the work.

sentences.zh: 又鑄銅為九州鼎及十二神，皆高一丈，各置其方。

translations.literal: Bronze was also cast into the Nine Provinces cauldrons and the Twelve Spirits, each one zhang high, and each was set in its proper direction.
translations.idiomatic: She also had bronze cast into the Nine Provinces cauldrons and the Twelve Spirit statues, each one zhang tall, and placed each in its proper quarter.

sentences.zh: 先是，河內老尼晝食一麻一米，夜則烹宰宴樂，畜弟子百餘人，淫穢靡所不為。

translations.literal: Earlier, an old nun of Henei ate one handful of hemp and one cup of rice by day, but by night slaughtered animals for feasting and revelry; she kept more than a hundred disciples and committed every sort of lewdness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there had been an old nun in Henei who ate a handful of hemp and a cup of rice by day, then by night feasted on slaughtered meat and wine. She kept more than a hundred disciples and indulged in every sort of debauchery.

sentences.zh: 武什方自言能合長年藥，太后遣乘驛於嶺南採藥。

translations.literal: Wu Shifang claimed he could compound elixirs of long life; the Empress Dowager sent him by post-horse to gather drugs in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifang claimed he could brew an elixir of longevity, and the Empress Dowager sent him south by imperial courier to gather herbs in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 及明堂火，尼入唁太后，太后怒叱之，曰：「汝常言能前知，何以不言明堂火？」

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall burned, the nun came to offer condolences to the Empress Dowager, who angrily rebuked her, saying, "You always claim foreknowledge—why did you not speak of the Bright Hall fire?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall burned, the nun came to offer condolences. The Empress Dowager furiously rebuked her: "You always claim you can see the future—why did you not warn me of this fire?"

sentences.zh: 因斥還河內，弟子及老胡等皆逃散。

translations.literal: She was driven back to Henei, and disciples and old barbarians alike all fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: She was expelled back to Henei, and her disciples and the foreign charlatans who followed her all fled.

sentences.zh: 又有發其奸者，太后乃復召尼還麟趾寺，弟子畢集，敕給使掩捕，盡獲之，皆沒為官婢。

translations.literal: When someone also exposed her crimes, the Empress Dowager summoned the nun back to Qilin Hoof Temple; when the disciples had all gathered, she ordered attendants to seize them by surprise—all were taken and made palace bondwomen.
translations.idiomatic: When her crimes were exposed, the Empress Dowager recalled the nun to Qilin Hoof Temple. Once all her disciples had gathered, she ordered attendants to seize them in a surprise raid. Every one was captured and made a government bondwoman.

sentences.zh: 什方還，至偃師，聞事露，自絞死。

translations.literal: Shifang returned; when he reached Yanshi and heard the affair had been exposed, he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shifang was on his way back when he reached Yanshi, learned the plot had been exposed, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以明堂火告廟，下制求直言。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the Bright Hall fire was reported to the ancestral temple, and an edict was issued seeking blunt counsel.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, the court reported the Bright Hall fire to the ancestral temple and issued an edict inviting frank criticism.

sentences.zh: 劉承慶上疏，以為：「火發既從麻主，後及總章，所營佛捨，恐勞無益，請罷之。

translations.literal: Liu Chengqing submitted a memorial, stating, "The fire began at the Mazhu shrine and afterward reached Zongzhang; the Buddhist halls being built will likely weary the people without profit—I request they be halted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chengqing submitted a memorial arguing that since the fire had begun at the Mazhu shrine and spread to Zongzhang, the Buddhist halls under construction would only exhaust the people to no purpose, and he asked that they be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 又，明堂所以統和天人，一旦焚毀，臣下何心猶為酺宴！

translations.literal: Moreover, the Bright Hall is where Heaven and man are harmonized; once it is burned in a day, how can your subjects' hearts still hold feasts!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Bright Hall is where Heaven and humanity are brought into harmony. Now that it lies in ashes, how can your officials still feast in good conscience?

sentences.zh: 憂喜相爭，傷於情性。

translations.literal: Grief and joy contend within one—this injures one's nature and feelings.
translations.idiomatic: To wrestle grief and celebration within the same breast wounds the heart.

sentences.zh: 又，陛下垂制博訪，許陳至理，而左史張鼎以為今既火流王屋，彌顯大周之祥，通事舍人逄敏奏稱，彌勒成道時有天魔燒宮，七寶台須臾散壞，斯實諂妄之邪言，非君臣之正論。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty by edict broadly sought counsel and permitted the utmost principles to be set forth, yet Left Historian Zhang Ding held that now that fire has flowed over the Royal Chamber, the Great Zhou's auspice is all the clearer; General Affairs Attendant Pang Min memorialized that when Maitreya attained the Way, heavenly demons burned the palace and the jeweled terrace was scattered in an instant—these are truly flatterers' perverse words, not the upright discourse of lord and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty invited honest counsel, yet Left Historian Zhang Ding claimed the blaze at the Royal Chamber only proved the Great Zhou's fortune. General Affairs Attendant Pang Min argued that when Maitreya attained enlightenment, demons burned his palace and his jeweled terrace crumbled in moments. These are sycophants' lies, not the honest counsel a ruler should hear.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下乾乾翼翼，無戾天人之心而興不急之役，則兆人蒙賴，福祿無窮。」

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty to be vigilant and reverent, not to go against the hearts of Heaven and man while raising unurgent works—then the myriad people will be blessed, and fortune and emolument without end."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to govern with vigilance and restraint, not to defy Heaven and the people's hearts by launching needless projects. Then the myriad people will prosper and your blessings will know no end."

sentences.zh: 獲嘉主簿彭城劉知幾表陳四事。

translations.literal: Liu Zhiji of Pengcheng, chief clerk of Huojia, memorialized setting forth four matters.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhiji of Pengcheng, chief clerk of Huojia County, submitted a memorial outlining four reforms.

sentences.zh: 其一以為：「皇業權輿，天地開闢，嗣君即位，黎元更始，則時藉非常之慶，以申再造之恩。

translations.literal: The first held that, "When imperial enterprise is in its first carriage, Heaven and Earth are newly opened, and a succeeding ruler takes the throne so the black-haired people begin anew, then the time calls for an extraordinary celebration to express the grace of renewed creation.
translations.idiomatic: First, he argued that when a dynasty is founded, Heaven and Earth are remade, and a new ruler ascends so the people begin anew, only then does the occasion warrant an extraordinary amnesty to celebrate renewal.

sentences.zh: 今六合清晏而赦令不息，近則一年再降，遠則每歲無遺，至於違法悖禮之徒，無賴不仁之輩，編戶則寇攘為業，當官則贓賄是求。

translations.literal: Now the six realms are tranquil yet amnesty edicts do not cease—lately twice in one year, and over time not one year omitted; as for those who violate law and defy ritual, the shiftless and unkind, registered households make brigandage their trade and officeholders seek bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now the realm is at peace while amnesties never cease—twice in a single year of late, and scarcely a year without one. Lawbreakers and the shameless take comfort: commoners turn to banditry, and officials to bribery.

sentences.zh: 而元日之朝，指期天澤，重陽之節，佇降皇恩，如其忖度，鹹果釋免。

translations.literal: Yet at the New Year's audience they count on Heaven's grace; at the Double Ninth they await the imperial favor—and as they reckon, all are indeed released.
translations.idiomatic: They count on New Year's Day for Heaven's mercy, on the Double Ninth for imperial favor—and as they expect, every crime is forgiven.

sentences.zh: 或有名垂結正，罪將斷決，竊行貨賄，方便規求，故致稽延，畢沾寬宥。

translations.literal: Some whose names hang at final judgment, whose crimes are about to be decided, secretly offer bribes and contrive delays, thus prolonging proceedings until all share in lenient pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Some whose cases are ready for execution bribe their way to delay after delay until the next amnesty washes them clean.

sentences.zh: 用使俗多頑悖，時罕廉隅，為善者不預恩光，作惡者獨承徼幸。

translations.literal: Hence custom grows stubborn and perverse, and the age rarely sees integrity; those who do good do not share in grace, while evildoers alone receive undeserved fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The result is a stubborn, corrupt age: the virtuous gain nothing, while criminals alone reap unearned mercy.

sentences.zh: 古語曰：『小人之幸，君子之不幸。」

translations.literal: An old saying runs, 'When petty men are fortunate, gentlemen are unfortunate.'
translations.idiomatic: As the ancients said, "When villains prosper, the upright suffer."

sentences.zh: 斯之謂也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: This is precisely such a case.

sentences.zh: 望陛下而今而後，頗節於赦，使黎氓知禁，奸宄肅清。」

translations.literal: I hope that from now on Your Majesty will somewhat restrain amnesties, so the black-haired people know prohibition and treachery is cleared away.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty henceforth to grant amnesties more sparingly, so the people learn restraint and crime is suppressed.

sentences.zh: 其二以為：「海內具僚九品以上，每歲逢赦，必賜階勳，至於朝野宴集，公私聚會，緋服眾於青衣，像板多於木笏；

translations.literal: The second held that, "Officials throughout the realm of the ninth rank and above, whenever an amnesty comes each year, invariably receive rank and merit awards; at court and countryside feasts, public and private gatherings, scarlet robes outnumber blue, and ivory tablets outnumber wooden tallies;
translations.idiomatic: Second, he argued that officials of the ninth rank and above receive promotions and honors at every annual amnesty. At court and in the provinces alike, scarlet robes outnumber blue, and ivory name-plates outnumber plain wooden ones.

sentences.zh: 皆榮非德舉，位罕才升，不知何者為妍蚩，何者為美惡。

translations.literal: all glory without merit, posts rarely filled by talent—one no longer knows who is fair or foul, who good or bad.
translations.idiomatic: Honor no longer follows merit, and office no longer follows talent. No one can tell the worthy from the worthless.

sentences.zh: 臣望自今以後，稍息私恩，使有善者逾效忠勤，無才者咸知勉勵。」

translations.literal: Your servant hopes that hereafter private favor will be somewhat stilled, so that those with merit will the more show loyalty and diligence, and those without talent will all know to strive.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty hereafter restrain such favoritism, so the capable are spurred to greater loyalty and the incompetent know they must earn their place.

sentences.zh: 其三以為：「陛下臨朝踐極，取士太廣，六品以下職事清官，遂乃方之土芥，比之沙礫，若遂不加沙汰，臣恐有穢皇風。」

translations.literal: The third held that, "Your Majesty, upon taking the throne, has recruited scholars too broadly; clerical posts of the sixth rank and below are treated like dust and gravel—if there is no further sifting, your servant fears the imperial wind will be stained.
translations.idiomatic: Third, he warned that since Your Majesty took the throne you have appointed officials too freely. Clerks of the sixth rank and below are treated like dirt. Without further winnowing, I fear the court's dignity will be soiled.

sentences.zh: 其四以為：「今之牧伯遷代太速，倏來忽往，蓬轉萍流，既懷苟縣之謀，何暇循良之政！

translations.literal: The fourth held that, "Today's regional governors are transferred too swiftly—coming in a flash and going in a flash, like tumbleweed and floating duckweed; since they harbor designs of temporary tenure, how can they find leisure for good governance!
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, he observed that prefects are rotated too quickly—here today, gone tomorrow, drifting like weeds on the water. Intent only on their next posting, how can they govern well?

sentences.zh: 望自今刺史非三歲以上不可遷官，仍明察功過，尤甄賞罰。」

translations.literal: I hope that henceforth prefects may not be transferred unless they have served three years or more, and that merit and fault be clearly examined, with rewards and punishments especially distinguished."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that prefects serve at least three years before transfer, and that their performance be rigorously judged, with clear rewards and punishments."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，太后頗嘉之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Empress Dowager was quite pleased with it.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was much pleased with the memorial.

sentences.zh: 是時官爵易得而法網嚴峻，故人競為趨進而多陷刑戮，知幾乃著《思慎賦》以刺時見志焉。

translations.literal: At that time offices and titles were easily gained while the legal net was severe, so men competed in advancement and many fell under punishment; Zhiji therefore composed 《Reflection on Caution》 to satirize the age and show his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Offices were easy to win but the law was merciless, and men scrambled for promotion only to fall to the executioner. Zhiji wrote 《Reflection on Caution》 to satirize the times and declare his principles.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以王孝傑為朔方道行軍總管，擊突厥。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Wang Xiaojie was made Commander of the Shuofang Circuit Field Army to strike the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Wang Xiaojie was appointed Commander of the Shuofang Circuit Field Army to campaign against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，己酉朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on the jiyou new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on the jiyou new moon, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 僧懷義益驕恣，太后惡之。

translations.literal: The monk Huaiyi grew ever more arrogant and unrestrained, and the Empress Dowager came to detest him.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huaiyi grew ever more arrogant, and the Empress Dowager grew to hate him.

sentences.zh: 既焚明堂，心不自安，言多不順；

translations.literal: Since he had burned the Bright Hall, his heart was ill at ease and his words often insolent;
translations.idiomatic: Having burned the Bright Hall, he was ill at ease and his speech turned defiant;

sentences.zh: 太后密選宮人有力者百餘人以防之。

translations.literal: the Empress Dowager secretly selected more than a hundred strong palace women to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: the Empress Dowager secretly chose more than a hundred strong palace women to keep watch on him.

sentences.zh: 壬子，執之於瑤光殿前樹下，使建昌王武攸寧師壯士毆殺之，送屍白馬寺，焚之以造塔。

translations.literal: On renzi, he was seized beneath the trees before Yaoguang Hall; Prince of Jianchang Wu Youning was made to lead strong men to beat him to death; the corpse was sent to White Horse Temple and burned to build a pagoda.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, he was seized beneath the trees before Yaoguang Hall. Prince of Jianchang Wu Youning led strongmen who beat him to death. His body was taken to White Horse Temple and burned to supply material for a pagoda.

sentences.zh: 甲子，太后去「慈氏越古」之號。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the Empress Dowager dropped the title "Kind Clan Surpassing Antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, the Empress Dowager relinquished the title "Kind Clan Surpassing Antiquity."

sentences.zh: 三月，丙辰，鳳閣侍郎、同平章事周允元薨。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingchen, Fengge Vice Minister and Associate Director of the Chancellery Zhou Yun'yuan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingchen, Fengge Vice Minister and Chancellor Zhou Yun'yuan died.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，天樞成，高一百五尺，逕十二尺，八面，各徑五尺。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Celestial Axis was completed, one hundred fifty chi high, twelve chi in circumference, eight faces, each five chi across.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the Celestial Axis pillar was completed—one hundred fifty chi tall, twelve chi in girth, with eight faces five chi wide each.

sentences.zh: 下為鐵山，周百七十尺，以銅為蟠龍麒麟縈繞之；

translations.literal: Below was an iron mountain one hundred seventy chi around, with coiled dragons and qilin in copper wound about it;
translations.idiomatic: Its base was an iron mountain one hundred seventy chi around, encircled by bronze coiled dragons and qilin;

sentences.zh: 上為騰雲承露盤，逕三丈，四龍人立捧火珠，高一丈。

translations.literal: above was a soaring-cloud dew-receiving dish three zhang across, with four dragons standing like men holding a fire pearl one zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: above it rose a cloud-borne dew basin three zhang wide, borne by four dragon figures standing upright and holding a fire pearl one zhang tall.

sentences.zh: 工人毛婆羅造模，武三思為文，刻百官及四夷酋長名，太后自書其榜曰「大周萬國頌德天樞」。

translations.literal: The craftsman Mao Boluo made the mold; Wu Sansi composed the inscription, carving the names of the hundred officials and the chieftains of the four barbarians; the Empress Dowager herself wrote the plaque: "Celestial Axis Commemorating the Virtue of the Great Zhou's Myriad States."
translations.idiomatic: The craftsman Mao Boluo cast the mold, Wu Sansi wrote the inscription, and the names of all officials and foreign chieftains were carved upon it. The Empress Dowager personally inscribed the plaque: "Celestial Axis Commemorating the Virtue of the Great Zhou's Myriad States."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛酉，吐蕃寇臨洮，以王孝傑為肅邊道行軍大總管以討之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinyou, Tibet raided Lintao; Wang Xiaojie was made Grand Commander of the Subian Circuit Field Army to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinyou, Tibet raided Lintao. Wang Xiaojie was appointed Grand Commander of the Subian Circuit Field Army to repel them.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲寅，太后合祭天地於南郊，加號天冊金輪大聖皇帝，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiayin, the Empress Dowager jointly sacrificed to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb, added the title Sage Emperor of the Heavenly Registers and Golden Wheel, pardoned all under Heaven, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiayin, the Empress Dowager offered joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb, took the title Sage Emperor of the Heavenly Registers and Golden Wheel, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，突厥默啜遣使請降，太后喜，冊授左衛大將軍、歸國公。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the Turk Mochuo sent envoys to request surrender; the Empress Dowager was pleased and enfeoffed him as General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and Duke Who Returned to the State.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the Turk khan Mochuo sent envoys to submit. The Empress Dowager was delighted and enfeoffed him as General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and Duke Who Returned to the State.

sentences.zh: 臘月，甲戌，太后發神都；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiaxu, the Empress Dowager departed the Divine Metropolis;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiaxu, the Empress Dowager departed the Divine Metropolis;

sentences.zh: 甲申，封神岳；

translations.literal: on jiashen, she performed the feng sacrifice on the sacred peak;
translations.idiomatic: on jiashen, she performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Song;

sentences.zh: 赦天下，改元萬歲登封，天下百姓無出今年租稅；

translations.literal: pardoned all under Heaven, changed the era name to Long Live the Ascension, and the common people throughout the realm owed no rent or tax this year;
translations.idiomatic: proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Long Live the Ascension, and exempted the common people from this year's rent and tax;

sentences.zh: 大酺九日。

translations.literal: a grand feast was held for nine days.
translations.idiomatic: and held a grand feast for nine days.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，禪於少室；

translations.literal: On dinghai, she performed the shan rite on Lesser Chamber;
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, she performed the shan rite on Lesser Chamber Peak;

sentences.zh: 己丑，御朝覲壇受賀；

translations.literal: on jichou, she took the Court Audience Altar to receive congratulations;
translations.idiomatic: on jichou, she took the Court Audience Altar to receive congratulations;

sentences.zh: 癸巳，還宮；

translations.literal: on guisi, she returned to the palace;
translations.idiomatic: on guisi, she returned to the palace;

sentences.zh: 甲午，謁太廟。

translations.literal: on jiawu, she visited the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: on jiawu, she visited the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 右千牛衛將軍安平王武攸緒，少有志行，恬澹寡慾，扈從封中岳還，即求棄官，隱於嵩山之陽。

translations.literal: General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, Prince of Ping'an Wu Youxu, from youth had resolve and conduct, was tranquil and of few desires; when he returned from escorting the feng rite on the central peak, he immediately sought to abandon office and retire on the southern slope of Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ping'an Wu Youxu, General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, had been principled and restrained from youth. When he returned from escorting the Empress Dowager's feng rite on Mount Song, he immediately asked to resign and live in seclusion on the mountain's southern slope.

sentences.zh: 太后疑其詐，許之，以觀其所為。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager suspected deception and consented, to observe what he would do.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager suspected a ruse but granted his request, intending to see what he would do.

sentences.zh: 攸緒遂優遊巖壑，冬居茅椒，夏居石室，一如山林之士。

translations.literal: Youxu then wandered at ease among cliffs and ravines, dwelling in thatched pepper-sheds in winter and stone chambers in summer, just like a man of mountain and forest.
translations.idiomatic: Youxu lived at ease among the peaks, in thatched huts in winter and stone chambers in summer, indistinguishable from a true hermit.

sentences.zh: 太后所賜及王公所遺野服器玩，攸緒一皆置之不用，塵埃凝積。

translations.literal: Rustic garments and curios bestowed by the Empress Dowager and presented by princes and dukes—Youxu set them all aside unused, and dust gathered thick upon them.
translations.idiomatic: The rustic clothes and curios the Empress Dowager and the princes sent him he left untouched until dust lay thick upon them.

sentences.zh: 買田使奴耕種，與民無異。

translations.literal: He bought fields and had slaves till them, no different from common folk.
translations.idiomatic: He bought farmland and had servants work it like any common farmer.

sentences.zh: 春，一月，甲寅，以婁師德為肅邊道行軍副總管，擊吐蕃。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jiayin, Lou Shide was made Deputy Grand Commander of the Subian Circuit Field Army to strike Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on jiayin, Lou Shide was appointed Deputy Grand Commander of the Subian Circuit Field Army to campaign against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以師德為左肅政大夫，知政事如故。

translations.literal: On jisi, Shide was made Left Censor-in-Chief and continued to oversee government affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Shide was made Left Censor-in-Chief while retaining his role in government.

sentences.zh: 改長安崇尊廟為太廟。

translations.literal: The Chongzun Temple in Chang'an was changed to the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Chongzun Temple in Chang'an was redesignated the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛巳，尊神岳天中王為神岳天中黃帝，靈妃為天中黃後；

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinsi, the Spirit Peak's King of the Heaven Within was honored as Yellow Emperor of the Spirit Peak Heaven Within, and the numinous consort as Yellow Empress of the Heaven Within;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinsi, the Spirit Peak's King of the Heaven Within was elevated to Yellow Emperor of the Spirit Peak Heaven Within, and his consort to Yellow Empress of the Heaven Within;

sentences.zh: 啟為齊聖皇帝；

translations.literal: Qi was made Sagely Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qi was posthumously titled Sagely Emperor;

sentences.zh: 封啟母神為玉京太后。

translations.literal: Qi's mother the spirit was enfeoffed as Jade Capital Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: and Qi's mother was enfeoffed as Jade Capital Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬寅，王孝傑、婁師德與吐蕃將論欽陵贊婆戰於素羅汗山，唐兵大敗；

translations.literal: In the third month, on renyin, Wang Xiaojie and Lou Shide fought the Tibetan generals Lun Qinling and Zanpo at Mount Suluohan; Tang troops were greatly defeated;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renyin, Wang Xiaojie and Lou Shide fought the Tibetan generals Lun Qinling and Zanpo at Mount Suluohan. The Tang army was routed;

sentences.zh: 孝傑坐免為庶人，師德貶原州員外司馬。

translations.literal: Xiaojie was demoted by statute and made a commoner; Shide was demoted to Outside Administrator in Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojie was stripped of rank and made a commoner; Shide was demoted to acting administrator in Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 師德因署移牒，驚曰：「官爵盡無邪？」

translations.literal: When Shide received the posted transfer document, he said in surprise, "Are office and rank all gone?"
translations.idiomatic: When Shide received his demotion notice, he exclaimed in surprise, "Gone—all my offices and honors?"

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「亦善，亦善！」

translations.literal: Then he said, "Also good, also good!"
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "Well enough, well enough!"

sentences.zh: 不復介意。

translations.literal: He gave the matter no further thought.
translations.idiomatic: And thought no more of it.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，新明堂成，高二百九十四尺，方三百尺，規模率小於舊。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the new Bright Hall was completed, two hundred ninety-four chi high and three hundred chi square, its scale on the whole smaller than the old.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, the new Bright Hall was completed—two hundred ninety-four chi tall and three hundred chi square, somewhat smaller than before.

sentences.zh: 上施金塗鐵鳳，高二丈，後為大風所損；

translations.literal: At the top was set an iron phoenix gilded with gold, two zhang high, which was later damaged by a great wind;
translations.idiomatic: At its summit stood a gilded iron phoenix two zhang tall, later broken by a great gale;

sentences.zh: 更為銅火珠，群龍捧之，號曰通天宮。

translations.literal: it was replaced with a bronze fire pearl, with a host of dragons holding it up, and the hall was titled Palace Reaching Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: it was replaced with a bronze fire pearl held aloft by dragons, and the hall was renamed Palace Reaching Heaven.

sentences.zh: 赦天下，改元萬歲通天。

translations.literal: All under Heaven was pardoned and the era name changed to Long Live and Penetrate Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Long Live and Penetrate Heaven.

sentences.zh: 大食請獻師子。

translations.literal: Dashi requested to present a lion.
translations.idiomatic: The Arabs requested to present a lion.

sentences.zh: 姚璹上疏，以為：「師子專食肉，遠道傳致，肉既難得，極為勞費。

translations.literal: Yao Shuang submitted a memorial, stating, "Lions eat only meat; to convey one from afar, meat is hard to obtain and the expense extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shuang objected in a memorial: "Lions eat only meat. To bring one from so far away, meat will be scarce and the cost enormous.

sentences.zh: 陛下鷹犬不蓄，漁獵悉停，豈容菲薄於身而厚給於獸！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty keeps no hawks or hounds and has halted all fishing and hunting—how can you be sparing toward yourself yet lavish toward beasts!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty keeps no hawks or hounds and has banned hunting—how can you deny yourself and lavish such care on a beast!"

sentences.zh: 乃卻之。

translations.literal: The gift was therefore declined.
translations.idiomatic: The gift was declined.

sentences.zh: 以檢校夏官侍郎孫元亨同平章事。

translations.literal: Acting Vice Minister of Summer Offices Sun Yuanheng was made Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Vice Minister of Summer Offices Sun Yuanheng was appointed Associate Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，壬子，營州契丹松漠都督李盡忠、歸誠州刺史孫萬榮舉兵反，攻陷營州，殺都督趙文翽。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on renzi, the Khitan of Yingzhou—Songmo Grand Protector Li Jinzhong and Guicheng Prefect Sun Wanrong—raised troops in rebellion, stormed Yingzhou, and killed Protector Zhao Wenyu.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on renzi, the Khitan leaders Li Jinzhong, Songmo Grand Protector, and Sun Wanrong, Prefect of Guicheng, rebelled, captured Yingzhou, and killed Protector Zhao Wenyu.

sentences.zh: 盡忠，萬榮之妹夫也，皆居於營州城側。

translations.literal: Jinzhong was Wanrong's brother-in-law; both lived beside Yingzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong was Wanrong's brother-in-law, and both lived beside the walls of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 文翽剛愎，契丹饑不加賑給，視酋長如奴僕，故二人怨而反。

translations.literal: Wenyu was obstinate; when the Khitan suffered famine he gave no relief, and treated chieftains like slaves—hence the two resented him and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu was arrogant and stubborn. When famine struck the Khitan he refused relief and treated their chiefs like servants. The two men rebelled in resentment.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，遣左鷹揚衛將軍曹仁師、右金吾衛大將軍張玄遇、左威衛大將軍李多祚、司農少卿麻仁節等二十八將討之。

translations.literal: On yichou, Left Upright Hawk Guard General Cao Renshi, Right Golden Crow Guard Grand General Zhang Xuan'yu, Left Awesome Guard Grand General Li Duozuo, Minister of Agriculture Junior Mentor Ma Renjie, and twenty-eight other generals were sent to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, twenty-eight generals including Cao Renshi of the Left Upright Hawk Guard, Zhang Xuan'yu of the Right Golden Crow Guard, Li Duozuo of the Left Awesome Guard, and Ma Renjie, Junior Mentor of the Ministry of Agriculture, were dispatched to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛亥，以春官尚書梁王武三思為榆關道安撫大使，姚璹副之，以備契丹。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinhai, Spring Offices Minister Prince of Liang Wu Sansi was made Pacification Commissioner of the Yuguan Circuit, with Yao Shuang as deputy, to guard against the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinhai, Prince of Liang Wu Sansi, Minister of Spring Offices, was made Pacification Commissioner of the Yuguan Circuit with Yao Shuang as his deputy, to guard against the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 改李盡忠為李盡滅，孫萬榮為孫萬斬。

translations.literal: Li Jinzhong was renamed Li Jinmie, and Sun Wanrong was renamed Sun Wanzhan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinzhong was officially renamed Li Jinmie, 'Exterminate to the End,' and Sun Wanrong was renamed Sun Wanzhan, 'Ten Thousand Slain.'

sentences.zh: 盡忠錄自稱無上可汗，據營州，以萬榮為前鋒，略地，所向皆下，旬日，兵至數萬，進圍檀州，清邊前軍副總管張九節擊卻之。

translations.literal: Jinzhong styled himself Supreme Qaghan, held Yingzhou, made Wanrong vanguard, and overran territory—wherever he went, all submitted; within ten days his troops reached tens of thousands; he advanced to besiege Tanzhou, and Deputy Forward Commander of the Clear Border Zhang Jiujie struck and repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong declared himself Supreme Qaghan, held Yingzhou, and sent Wanrong as vanguard. His armies swept all before them; within ten days he had tens of thousands of men. He advanced to besiege Tanzhou, but Deputy Forward Commander Zhang Jiujie drove him back.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁酉，曹仁師、張玄遇、麻仁節與契丹戰於硤石谷，唐兵大敗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on dingyou, Cao Renshi, Zhang Xuan'yu, and Ma Renjie fought the Khitan at Xiashi Valley; Tang troops were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dingyou, Cao Renshi, Zhang Xuan'yu, and Ma Renjie met the Khitan at Xiashi Valley. The Tang army was routed.

sentences.zh: 先是，契丹破營州，獲唐俘數百，囚之地牢，聞唐兵將至，使守牢□紿之曰：「吾輩家屬，饑寒不能自存，唯俟官軍至即降耳。」

translations.literal: Earlier, the Khitan had taken Ying Prefecture and captured several hundred Tang prisoners, whom they imprisoned in a dungeon. When they heard that Tang troops were approaching, they had the dungeon guards deceive them, saying: "Our families, starving and freezing, cannot support themselves; we are only waiting for the government army to arrive, and then we will surrender at once."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the Khitan seized Ying Prefecture they took several hundred Tang captives and locked them in a dungeon. Hearing that Tang forces were on the way, they had the jailers deceive the prisoners: "Our kin are starving in the cold and cannot survive on their own—we are only waiting for the government troops to come so we can surrender at once."

sentences.zh: 既而契丹引出其俘，飼以糠粥，慰勞之曰：「吾養汝則無食，殺汝又不忍，今縱汝去。」

translations.literal: Thereupon the Khitan led the prisoners out, fed them bran porridge, and comforted them, saying: "If we keep you we have no food; if we kill you we cannot bear it—now we release you to go."
translations.idiomatic: Then the Khitan brought the captives out, fed them millet gruel, and consoled them: "Keeping you alive leaves us nothing to eat; killing you we cannot bear—go, we release you now."

sentences.zh: 遂釋之。

translations.literal: They then released them.
translations.idiomatic: And so they let them go.

sentences.zh: 俘至幽州，具言其狀，諸軍聞之，爭欲先入。

translations.literal: The captives reached You Prefecture and reported the full situation; on hearing it, the various armies vied to enter first.
translations.idiomatic: The freed men reached You Prefecture and told the whole story. Every unit, hearing it, raced to be first into battle.

sentences.zh: 至黃獐谷，虜又遣老弱迎降，故遺老牛瘦馬於道側。

translations.literal: When they reached Huangzhang Valley, the barbarians again sent the old and weak to welcome them in surrender, and deliberately left old oxen and thin horses by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangzhang Valley the enemy again sent elders and weaklings out to feign surrender, and purposely abandoned old oxen and scrawny horses along the road.

sentences.zh: 仁師等三軍棄步卒，將騎兵輕進。

translations.literal: Renshi and the other three armies abandoned their foot soldiers and led their cavalry forward lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Renshi and the other three commands left their infantry behind and pushed ahead with cavalry alone.

sentences.zh: 契丹設伏橫擊之，飛索以絲□玄遇、仁節，生獲之，將卒死者填山谷，鮮有脫者。

translations.literal: The Khitan laid an ambush and struck them from the flank; flying ropes of silk bound Xuan'yu and Renjie and took them alive; officers and men who died filled the valleys, and few escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sprang an ambush and cut them off from the flank. Silk snares flew up and bound Zhang Xuan'yu and Ma Renjie alive; dead officers and men choked the valleys, and almost none got away.

sentences.zh: 契丹得軍印，詐為牒，令玄遇等署之，牒總管燕匪石、宗懷昌等云：「官軍已破賊，若至營州，軍將皆斬，兵不敘勳。」

translations.literal: The Khitan obtained the army seals, forged dispatches, and had Xuan'yu and others sign them. The dispatches to the generals Yan Feishi, Zong Huaichang, and others read: "The government army has already broken the bandits. If you reach Ying Prefecture, the army officers will all be executed and the troops will receive no record of merit."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan seized the army seals, forged orders, and forced Xuan'yu and the rest to sign them. The forged messages to the commanders Yan Feishi and Zong Huaichang declared: "The government forces have already routed the rebels. If you reach Ying Prefecture, every officer will be executed and the soldiers will receive no rewards."

sentences.zh: 匪石等得牒，晝夜兼行，不遑寢食以赴之，士馬疲弊；

translations.literal: Feishi and the others received the dispatches, traveled day and night without pause for sleep or food to hurry to the spot, and men and horses were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Feishi and his colleagues took the orders at face value and marched day and night without rest or proper meals; men and horses were spent.

sentences.zh: 契丹伏兵於中道邀之，全軍皆沒。

translations.literal: The Khitan lay in ambush midway and intercepted them; the whole army was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan troops waiting along the road fell on them; the entire force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 九月，制：「天下系囚及士庶家奴驍勇者，官償其直，發以擊契丹。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict stated: "Prisoners under sentence throughout the realm and daring bondsmen among scholars and commoners—the government shall compensate their value and send them to attack the Khitan."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict declared: "All convicts in custody and any sturdy household slaves among the people shall be purchased at state expense and dispatched against the Khitan."

sentences.zh: 初令山東近邊諸州置武騎團兵，以同州刺史建安王武攸宜為右武威衛大將軍，充清邊道行軍大總管，以討契丹。

translations.literal: For the first time, the near-frontier prefectures east of the mountains were ordered to establish Military Cavalry regiment troops. Prince of Jian'an Wu Youyi, prefect of Tong Prefecture, was made Grand General of the Right Majestic Martial Guard and appointed Commander-in-Chief on campaign along the Qingbian route to attack the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The edict also ordered frontier prefectures east of the mountains to raise mounted regiments known as Military Cavalry. Wu Youyi, Prince of Jian'an and prefect of Tong, became Grand General of the Right Majestic Martial Guard and Commander-in-Chief on the Qingbian campaign against the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 右拾遺陳子昂為攸宜府參謀，上疏曰：「恩制免天下罪人及募諸色奴充兵討擊契丹，此乃捷急之計，非天子之兵。

translations.literal: Right Petitioner Chen Zi'ang served as staff adviser in Youyi's headquarters and submitted a memorial, saying: "The grace-edict that pardons all criminals under Heaven and recruits bondsmen of every sort to fill the ranks to attack the Khitan—this is a plan of desperate haste, not the army of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zi'ang, Right Remonstrance Official and adviser on Youyi's staff, memorialized: "Pardoning every criminal in the empire and pressing slaves of every description into service against the Khitan is an emergency trick, not the sovereign's own army.

sentences.zh: 且比來刑獄久清，罪人全少，奴多怯弱，不慣征行，縱其募集，未足可用。

translations.literal: Moreover, of late the prisons have long been clear and criminals are very few; bondsmen are mostly timid and weak and unaccustomed to campaigning. Even if recruited, they would scarcely suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the courts have been quiet for years—real convicts are scarce—and most slaves are timid, unused to war. Even if you conscript them, they will not be enough.

sentences.zh: 況當今天下忠臣勇士，萬分未用其一，契丹小孽，假命待誅，何勞免罪贖奴，損國大體！

translations.literal: Moreover, throughout the realm today loyal ministers and brave warriors—not one in ten thousand has been used. The Khitan are a petty evil awaiting execution by borrowed mandate; why trouble to pardon crimes and ransom bondsmen, damaging the great structure of the state!
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile loyal soldiers and able men stand unused by the tens of thousands, while this petty Khitan scourge merely awaits the axe. Why demean the state by freeing criminals and buying slaves?

sentences.zh: 臣恐此策不可威示天下。」

translations.literal: I fear this policy cannot inspire awe throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: I fear such a policy will not awe the empire."

sentences.zh: 丁巳，突厥寇涼州，執都督許欽明。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the Turks raided Liang Prefecture and seized Supervisor Xu Qinming.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the Turks struck Liang Prefecture and captured Area Commander Xu Qinming.

sentences.zh: 欽明，紹之曾孫也；

translations.literal: Qinming was a great-grandson of Xu Shao;
translations.idiomatic: Qinming was a great-grandson of Xu Shao.

sentences.zh: 時出按部，突厥數萬奄至城下，欽明拒戰，為所虜。

translations.literal: At the time he was out inspecting his circuit when tens of thousands of Turks suddenly arrived below the walls; Qinming resisted but was captured.
translations.idiomatic: He was away on circuit inspection when tens of thousands of Turks appeared before the walls. Qinming fought back but was taken.

sentences.zh: 欽明兄欽寂，時為龍山軍討擊副使，與契丹戰於崇州，軍敗，被擒。

translations.literal: Qinming's elder brother Qinji, then Deputy Commissioner for Punitive Campaigns of the Longshan Army, fought the Khitan at Chong Prefecture; the army was defeated and he was taken.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Qinji, then deputy commander of the Longshan punitive army, met the Khitan at Chong Prefecture, lost, and was captured.

sentences.zh: 虎將圍安東，令欽寂說其屬城未下者。

translations.literal: General Hu besieged Andong and had Qinji persuade the subordinate cities that had not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan general Hu besieged Andong and ordered Qinji to talk the remaining cities into surrender.

sentences.zh: 安東都護裴玄珪在城中，欽寂謂曰：「狂賊天殃，滅在朝夕，公但勵兵謹守以全忠節。」

translations.literal: Protector-General of Andong Pei Xuangui was in the city. Qinji said to him: "The mad bandits are heaven's scourge; their destruction is within days. Your Lordship need only encourage the troops and hold fast carefully to preserve your loyal integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Protector-General Pei Xuangui held the city. Qinji told him: "These mad rebels carry heaven's curse—their end is near. Stir your men, defend steadfastly, and keep your honor intact."

sentences.zh: 虜殺之。

translations.literal: The barbarians killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then executed him.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃復遣使請和親，太后遣右武衛冑曹參軍貴鄉郭元振往察其宜。

translations.literal: Tubo again sent envoys to request marriage alliance; the Empress Dowager sent Guo Yuanzhen of Guixiang, Right Martial Guard Armoury Staff Officer, to investigate what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet again asked for a marriage alliance. Empress Dowager Wu sent Guo Yuanzhen of Guixiang, a staff officer of the Right Martial Guard, to weigh the proposal.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃將論欽陵請罷安西四鎮戍兵，並求分十姓突厥之地。

translations.literal: The Tibetan general Lun Qinling asked to abolish garrison troops of the Four Garrisons of Anxi and also sought a division of the lands of the Ten Surnames of the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetan commander Lun Qinling demanded withdrawal of Tang garrisons in the Four Protectorates of Anxi and a share of the Ten Surnames Turkic lands.

sentences.zh: 元振曰：「四鎮、十姓與吐蕃種類本殊，今請罷唐兵，豈非有兼併之志乎？」

translations.literal: Yuanzhen said: "The Four Garrisons and Ten Surnames are fundamentally of a different stock from Tubo. Now you ask to withdraw Tang troops—do you not have designs of annexation?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen replied: "The Four Garrisons and the Ten Surnames are not your people at all. If you want Tang soldiers gone, is that not a plan to swallow them?"

sentences.zh: 欽陵曰：「吐蕃苟貪土地，欲為邊患，則東侵甘、涼，豈肯規利於萬里之外邪！」

translations.literal: Qinling said: "If Tubo were greedy for territory and wished to be a frontier menace, it would invade east into Gan and Liang—how would it scheme for profit ten thousand li away!"
translations.idiomatic: Qinling answered: "If we craved land and meant to raid the frontier, we would strike Gan and Liang to the east—why chase gain ten thousand li off?"

sentences.zh: 乃遣使者隨元振入請之。

translations.literal: Envoys were then sent to follow Yuanzhen in and present the request.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent envoys back with Yuanzhen to press the petition at court.

sentences.zh: 朝廷疑未決，元振上疏，以為：「欽陵求罷兵割地，此乃利害之機，誠不可輕舉措也。

translations.literal: The court was uncertain and had not yet decided; Yuanzhen submitted a memorial, holding that: "Qinling's request to withdraw troops and cede territory is a matter of profit and harm; it truly must not be handled lightly.
translations.idiomatic: The court hesitated. Yuanzhen wrote: "Qinling's demand to pull troops and carve up territory is a hinge of profit and loss—it must not be decided rashly.

sentences.zh: 今若直拒其善意，則為邊患必深。

translations.literal: If we now flatly refuse his good intent, the frontier menace will surely deepen.
translations.idiomatic: Reject his offer outright and the border trouble will surely worsen.

sentences.zh: 四鎮之利遠，甘、涼之害近，不可不深圖也。

translations.literal: The benefit of the Four Garrisons is far; the harm to Gan and Liang is near—this cannot but be deeply plotted.
translations.idiomatic: Gain in the Four Garrisons lies far away; injury to Gan and Liang is close at hand—this demands deep calculation.

sentences.zh: 宜以計緩之，使其和望未絕則善矣。

translations.literal: It is fitting to use stratagem to slow him, so that his hope for peace is not severed—then it will be well.
translations.idiomatic: Better to stall him by craft and keep his hope of peace alive.

sentences.zh: 彼四鎮、十姓，吐蕃之所甚欲也，而青海、吐谷渾，亦國家之要地也，今報之宜曰：『四鎮、十姓之地，本無用於中國，所以遣兵戍之，欲以鎮撫西域，分吐蕃之勢，使不得並力東侵也。

translations.literal: Those Four Garrisons and Ten Surnames are what Tubo desires most, while Qinghai and the Tuyuhun are also crucial lands of the state. The reply should now say: 'The lands of the Four Garrisons and Ten Surnames are fundamentally of no use to China; the reason troops were sent to garrison them was to pacify and comfort the Western Regions, divide Tubo's strength, and keep it from combining forces to invade east.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Garrisons and Ten Surnames are what Tibet wants most; Qinghai and the Tuyuhun are vital to us. Answer thus: 'Those western posts are useless to China in themselves—we garrison them only to steady the Western Regions, split Tibetan power, and stop you from concentrating for an eastern attack.

sentences.zh: 今若果無東侵之志，當歸我吐谷渾諸部及青海故地，則五俟斤部亦當以歸吐蕃。』

translations.literal: If you truly have no intent to invade east, you should return to us the various tribes of the Tuyuhun and the former lands of Qinghai; then the Five Irkin Clans should also be returned to Tubo."
translations.idiomatic: If you truly mean no eastern aggression, restore our Tuyuhun tribes and the old Qinghai lands—then the Five Irkin divisions may go to Tibet."

sentences.zh: 如此則足以塞欽陵之口，而亦未與之絕也。

translations.literal: This would suffice to silence Qinling's mouth and yet not break with him entirely.
translations.idiomatic: That would shut Qinling up yet keep the door open.

sentences.zh: 若欽陵小有乖違，則曲在彼矣。

translations.literal: If Qinling shows the slightest breach, the fault will lie on his side.
translations.idiomatic: If Qinling balks even slightly, the blame is his.

sentences.zh: 且四鎮、十姓款附歲久，今未察其情之向背，事之利害，遙割而棄之，恐傷諸國之心，非所以御四夷也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the Four Garrisons and Ten Surnames have submitted in good faith for many years. To cut them off and abandon them from afar without yet discerning the disposition of their hearts or the profit and harm of the matter would fear to wound the hearts of the various states—not the way to control the Four Barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, those regions have been loyal for years. To lop them off without knowing where loyalties lie would break the faith of many states—that is no way to rule the frontier peoples."

sentences.zh: 太后從之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wu agreed.

sentences.zh: 元振又上言：「吐蕃百姓疲於徭戍，早願和親；

translations.literal: Yuanzhen further submitted: "The people of Tubo are weary of corvée and frontier garrison duty and have long wished for marriage alliance;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen added: "Tibetan commoners are worn out by labor and garrison duty and have long wanted peace through marriage;

sentences.zh: 欽陵利於統兵專制，獨不欲歸款。

translations.literal: Qinling profits from command of troops and sole power; he alone does not wish to return to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Qinling thrives on holding armies and ruling alone—he alone refuses reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 若國家歲發和親使，而欽陵常不從命，則彼國之人怨欽陵日深。

translations.literal: If the state sends marriage-alliance envoys every year while Qinling constantly does not comply, then the people of that country will resent Qinling daily more deeply,
translations.idiomatic: If the court sends betrothal missions every year and Qinling keeps refusing, his own people will hate him more each day,

sentences.zh: 望國恩日甚，設欲大舉其徒，固亦難矣。

translations.literal: their longing for the state's grace daily greater. Even if he wished to mobilize his host in full, it would indeed be difficult.
translations.idiomatic: while their longing for Tang favor grows. Even if he tried to rally the masses for war, it would be hard.

sentences.zh: 斯亦離間之漸，可使其上下猜阻，禍亂內興矣。」

translations.literal: This too is the gradual way of sowing discord—one may make their upper and lower ranks suspicious and obstructive, and strife arise within."
translations.idiomatic: That is a slow form of division—let suspicion grow between ruler and ruled until turmoil rises within."

sentences.zh: 太后深然之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wu strongly approved.

sentences.zh: 元振名震，以字行。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen's personal name was Zhen; he was known by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: His given name was Zhen; he went by his style name Yuanzhen.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以并州長史王方慶為鸞台侍郎，與殿中監萬年李道廣並同平章事。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Wang Fangqing, prefect of Bing, was appointed Vice Minister of the Luan Terrace, and Li Daoguang of Wannian, Palace Supervisor, was made Fellow Grand Councilors with equal standing.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Wang Fangqing, Bingzhou prefect, became Vice Minister of the Luan Terrace, and Li Daoguang of Wannian, a palace supervisor, joined him as co–Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 突厥默啜請為太后子，並為其女求昏，悉歸河西降戶，帥其部眾為國討契丹。

translations.literal: The Turk Mojie requested to become the Empress Dowager's son and also sought marriage for his daughter, that all surrendered households west of the He be returned, and that he lead his tribes to campaign for the state against the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The Turk khaghan Mojie asked to be adopted as Empress Dowager Wu's son, sought a bride for his daughter, demanded return of all surrendered households west of the Yellow River, and offered to lead his tribes against the Khitan for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 太后遣豹韜衛大將軍閻知微、左衛郎將攝司賓卿田歸道冊授默啜左衛大將軍、遷善可汗。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager sent Grand General of the Leopard-Tiger Guard Yan Zhiwei and Left Guard Gentleman Lang, acting Minister of Guests Tian Guidao, to invest Mojie as Grand General of the Left Guard and Qianshan Khaghan.
translations.idiomatic: She sent Grand General Yan Zhiwei of the Leopard-Tiger Guard and Tian Guidao, Left Guard officer acting as Minister of Guests, to invest Mojie as Grand General of the Left Guard and Khaghan Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 知微，立德之孫；

translations.literal: Zhiwei was a grandson of Yan Lide;
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwei was a grandson of Yan Lide.

sentences.zh: 歸道，仁會之子也。

translations.literal: Guidao was a son of Tian Renhui.
translations.idiomatic: Guidao was a son of Tian Renhui.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛卯，契丹李盡忠卒，孫萬榮代領其眾。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinmao, the Khitan Li Jinzhong died and Sun Wanrong succeeded to command his hosts.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinmao, the Khitan leader Li Jinzhong died; Sun Wanrong took command of his forces.

sentences.zh: 突厥默啜乘間襲松漠，虜盡忠、萬榮妻子而去。

translations.literal: The Turk Mojie seized the interval to raid Songmo and carried off Jinzhong's and Wanrong's wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Mojie seized the moment to strike Songmo and carried off the wives and children of Jinzhong and Wanrong.

sentences.zh: 太后進拜默啜為頡跌利施大單于、立功報國可汗。
