translations.literal: The Empress Dowager advanced Mojie to Great Khaghan Tuildishi and Khaghan Meritorious Service to the State.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wu promoted him to Great Khaghan Tuildishi, Khaghan Who Serves the State with Merit.

sentences.zh: 孫萬榮收合餘眾，軍勢復振，遣別帥駱務整、何阿小為前鋒，攻陷冀州，殺刺史陸寶積，屠吏居數千人；

translations.literal: Sun Wanrong gathered the remnant hosts; army morale revived. He sent lieutenants Luo Wuzheng and He Axiao as vanguard, who took Ji Prefecture, killed Prefect Lu Baoji, and slaughtered several thousand officials and residents;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wanrong rallied the survivors and his army surged again. He sent the lieutenants Luo Wuzheng and He Axiao ahead; they seized Ji Prefecture, killed Prefect Lu Baoji, and massacred thousands of officials and townspeople.

sentences.zh: 又攻瀛州，河北震動。

translations.literal: They also attacked Ying Prefecture, and Hebei was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on toward Ying Prefecture, and all Hebei trembled.

sentences.zh: 制起彭澤令狄仁傑為魏州刺史。

translations.literal: By edict, Di Renjie, magistrate of Pengze, was summoned to be prefect of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled Di Renjie, magistrate of Pengze, to serve as prefect of Wei.

sentences.zh: 前刺史獨孤思莊畏契丹猝至，悉驅百姓入城，繕修守備。

translations.literal: The former prefect Dugu Sizhuang, fearing a sudden Khitan arrival, drove all the common people into the city and repaired defenses.
translations.idiomatic: The outgoing prefect Dugu Sizhuang, dreading a sudden Khitan strike, had driven every farmer behind the walls and feverishly strengthened defenses.

sentences.zh: 仁傑至，悉遣還農，曰：「賊猶在遠，何煩如是！

translations.literal: When Renjie arrived he sent them all back to their fields, saying: "The bandits are still far off—why trouble yourselves thus!
translations.idiomatic: Renjie, on arriving, sent them all back to their fields, saying: "The rebels are still far away—why all this panic?

sentences.zh: 萬一賊來，吾自當之。」

translations.literal: If by chance the bandits come, I myself will meet them."
translations.idiomatic: If they do come, I will face them myself."

sentences.zh: 百姓大悅。

translations.literal: The common people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The people were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 時契丹入寇，軍書填委，夏官郎中硤石姚元崇剖析如流，皆有條理，太后奇之，擢為夏官侍郎。

translations.literal: At this time the Khitan were invading and military dispatches piled up; Yao Yuanchong of Xiashi, Master in the Bureau of Summer Affairs, analyzed them like flowing water, all with clear order. The Empress Dowager marveled and promoted him to Vice Minister of Summer Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With Khitan raids flooding the offices with reports, Yao Yuanchong of Xiashi, a director in the Ministry of War, sorted each dispatch with fluent clarity. Empress Dowager Wu was impressed and made him vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 太后思徐有功用法平，擢拜左台殿中侍御史，遠近聞者無不相賀。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager remembered Xu Yougong's even-handed use of law and appointed him Left Terrace Attending Palace Censor; near and far, those who heard rejoiced alike.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering Xu Yougong's fair administration of justice, Empress Dowager Wu appointed him Attending Censor of the Left Terrace; celebrants stretched from the capital to the provinces.

sentences.zh: 鹿城主簿宗城潘好禮著論，稱有功蹈道依仁，固守誠節，不以貴賤死生易其操履。

translations.literal: Pan Haoli of Zongcheng, chief clerk of Lucheng, wrote a treatise praising Yougong for treading the Way and leaning on benevolence, holding fast to loyal integrity, and not changing his conduct for rank, low estate, life, or death.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Haoli, chief clerk of Lucheng in Zongcheng, published an essay praising Yougong for walking the Way, resting on humaneness, and holding his integrity whether honored or disgraced, alive or dead.

sentences.zh: 設客問曰：「徐公於今誰與為比？」

translations.literal: He posed a guest who asked: "With whom may Lord Xu be compared today?"
translations.idiomatic: In it a guest asks: "To whom may Lord Xu be compared in our age?"

sentences.zh: 主人曰：「四海至廣，人物至多，或匿跡韜光，僕不敢誣，若所聞見，則一人而已，當於古人中求之。」

translations.literal: The host said: "Within the Four Seas is vast and persons are many; some hide their traces and veil their light—I dare not speak falsely. Of those I have heard and seen, there is but one man, and he should be sought among the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: The host answers: "The world is wide and full of hidden talent—I will not invent names. Of men I have truly known, there is only one, and he belongs among the ancients."

sentences.zh: 客曰：「何如張釋之？」

translations.literal: The guest said: "How about Zhang Shizhi?"
translations.idiomatic: The guest says: "What of Zhang Shizhi?"

sentences.zh: 主人曰：「釋之所行者甚易，徐公所行者甚難。

translations.literal: The host said: "What Shizhi practiced was very easy; what Lord Xu practiced was very hard. Between hard and easy, superior and inferior are plain.
translations.idiomatic: The host replies: "Zhang Shizhi's path was easy; Lord Xu's was hard. Between easy and hard, merit shows.

sentences.zh: 難易之間，優劣見矣。

translations.literal: Between difficulty and ease, superiority and inferiority are revealed.
translations.idiomatic: Between the two, high and low stand clear.

sentences.zh: 張公逢漢文之時，天下無事，至如盜高廟玉環及渭橋驚馬，守法而已，豈不易哉！

translations.literal: Lord Zhang met Emperor Wen of Han when all under Heaven was untroubled; matters such as stealing the jade ring from the High Temple or startling horses at Wei Bridge required only keeping the law—was that not easy!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shizhi served Emperor Wen when the empire was at peace; cases like theft of the High Temple's jade ring or a stampede at Wei Bridge needed only the letter of the law—was that not easy?

sentences.zh: 徐公逢革命之秋，屬惟新之運，唐朝遺老，或包藏禍心，使人主有疑。

translations.literal: Lord Xu met the season of revolution and the fortune of renewal; old retainers of the Tang might harbor evil designs and make the sovereign suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Xu lived in a time of upheaval and new mandates; Tang loyalists still nursed treason, and the throne itself was wary.

sentences.zh: 如周興、來俊臣，乃堯年之四凶也，崇飾惡言以誣盛德；

translations.literal: Men like Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen were the Four Evils of Yao's age, heaping ornate wicked words to slander flourishing virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Men like Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen were the Four Evils of legend, piling slander on the righteous;

sentences.zh: 而徐公守死善道，深相明白，幾陷囹圄，數掛網羅，此吾子所聞，豈不難哉！」

translations.literal: yet Lord Xu held to death in the good Way, explained clearly at great depth, nearly fell into prison, and was repeatedly caught in nets—this your servant has heard; is it not hard!"
translations.idiomatic: yet Lord Xu clung to justice unto death, spoke truth at peril, nearly died in prison, and was snared again and again—as you have heard, was that not hard?"

sentences.zh: 客曰：「使為司刑卿，乃得展其才矣。」

translations.literal: The guest said: "If he were made Minister of Punishments, then he could fully display his talent."
translations.idiomatic: The guest says: "Make him Minister of Punishments and his talent would finally show."

sentences.zh: 主人曰：「吾子徒見徐公用法平允，謂可置司刑；

translations.literal: The host said: "Your servant only sees Lord Xu's even-handed use of law and thinks him fit for the office of Minister of Punishments;
translations.idiomatic: The host answers: "You see only his fair judgments and think him fit for the Ministry of Punishments;

sentences.zh: 僕睹其人，方寸之地，何所不容，若其用之，何事不可，豈直司刑而已哉！

translations.literal: this servant beholds the man—in a space a cun square, nothing he cannot contain; if put to use, nothing he could not do—how is it only Minister of Punishments!
translations.idiomatic: I see a heart that holds all within a thumb's breadth—given office, there is nothing he could not do. Why limit him to punishments alone?
